facts: The reservation branch requires a live caller. Shared authentication, halt/killswitch, kiosk and receipt gates are separate wrapper obligations; this facet closes only reservation/item authority.

Item lookup trims the submitted slug, scans work_items then work_items_archive, and matches the exact slug; it never resolves an old opaque ID to a new name. Archived items remain eligible for this metadata access.

Visibility is USER, the stored owner or creator node, a strict ancestor of owner (or creator while unowned), an explicit participant, or the named reviewer. Stored actor objects resolve by node string here; this is the legacy rule, not a claim of born-identity fencing.

Ancestry reads parent links from the anchor toward USER with a cycle guard. Org visibility alone grants no docket access. The item owner/creator/reviewer, participants, and necessary parent links are the predicate read set.

The reservation adapter converts both missing and unreadable item lookup to false; its refusal is identical for either. Naming a resource permits only the contention projection of HELD rows, never item-read or mutation authority.

Renew/release/land require exact reservation ownership, not merely item visibility. Recover of a HELD claim instead checks stored lease/heartbeat and owner liveness, and returns only contention metadata to an unrelated caller.

A release successor must be live and able to read a nonempty associated item. These checks are necessary but not sufficient: post_mail also enforces addressing, and its refusal must roll back the entire release.

The source is the P02 probe tools/p02_operation_contacts.py (landed on v3 at b6568a1; method and limits in docs/state-system/p02-operation-contacts.md; P02 artifact r3 on p02-capture-per-operation-contacts-for-the-four, sha256 25cca77ab5b277627b03daf5d2b24c8a65b0bd5cf6599661f94ea7bfe33b10cb). It was re-run independently, and every observed fact below is asserted by tests/test_state_p02_contact_facets.py, which runs the same probe.

The complete read set of one public call is recorded as ONE UNION per call, not split into dispatch, authentication and receipt phases (S2b ruling R2, accepted by review). Cold: doc, log_d, log_l, meta and nodes. Warm: doc, meta and nodes. All on the primary org store only; no sidecar store is read, and no sidecar or provider file is opened.

Phase attribution is BOUNDED by separately observed rows, not measured inside a successful call. 401: 0 statements (the token gate refuses before the census). 403: 0 statements (_agent_identity checks the cached snapshot and makes no statement). The halt/killswitch refusal before the lock reads doc, meta and nodes (5 statements) through halt.blocked.

Receipt admission reads the receipts tables. A keyed replay reads doc, log_l and meta and returns before the domain helper. A fresh keyed read reads meta and nodes, then writes its receipt. The domain predicate read sets per variant remain the source-level facts of the reservation facets; this facet adds the observed physical tables.

Limits carried from P02: statements only (no rows examined, pages, physical IO or database lock wait; the document-lock wait is in each record's profile). Tables come from the harness's SQL-text map onto the stores' own sqlite_master names, so contacts are table-granular. SQLite's own file IO is native and unobserved. One synthetic fixture set, in one process. Native or PostgreSQL contacts are outside this legacy facet.

Both public names are TX_POST for every action, including the domain reads list/landing/overlap. The call runs in the resident write cycle (store.write_org under DOC_LOCK), which always ends in save_org, even for a domain read. What each outcome actually commits is measured below.

Measured on disposable SQLite with the committed document read cold (resident copy evicted): an unkeyed read commits nothing; any refusal commits nothing (domain or addressing 422, keyed conflict 409, halt/killswitch 409 before the lock); a keyed replay returns before the save and commits nothing.

A keyed read commits op_receipts and op_receipts_meta only. A keyed renew also commits reservations. A keyed release with a successor commits reservations, mail, mail_log, events, lifecycle, audiences (the first grant to a deeper report), the receiver node's mail_seq, op_receipts and op_receipts_meta, then drives one ping.

_op_file appends the receipt as the last mutation before save_org, so the receipt and its effect commit together or not at all. opreceipts.append advances meta.seq on every append; past CEILING it evicts down to TRIM_TO and moves meta.from_ms past the largest evicted mint time. opreceipts.custody/witness and _op_inflight change only in-process state.

Before the transaction the route sets a request-profiling label, a stateprobe label and an attempt-census classification. These are in-memory. The reservation names are not MANAGED_WAIT_TOOLS, so no tool-wait sidecar row and no seat_id mint occur.

The one durable diagnostic write is the slow-request trace. When handler time reaches slowtrace.THRESHOLD_MS (ORGTREE_SLOW_TRACE_MS, default 500), the access middleware calls slowtrace.emit. If <data>/diagnostics/slow-requests.jsonl is over its size cap (ORGTREE_SLOW_TRACE_MAX_KB, default 4096), emit first renames it to a single .1 sibling, replacing and so discarding any older .1. It then appends one row: route, method, status, timings, byte count and allowlisted profile fields, with no tool arguments. emit swallows its own errors, so it never fails the request. The profile-timing sink is an in-memory deque plus stdout.

Physical SQL statements, table and row fan-out, and waits behind these section changes belong to the unresolved `contacts` facet (P02). Pinned by tests/test_state_reservation_boundary.py (wrapper outcome table, slow-trace privacy, keyed read/replay/refusal and failure cases).

Target conflict sets must preserve predicates without replacing DOC_LOCK by a mandatory global row.
Shared-resource and original integration-key conflicts differ from physical engine waits.

facts: action = str(args.get('action') or '').strip().lower(); the alias reaches the identical adapter.
_safe and _contention are separate allowlisted result projections; no arbitrary args echoed.
Declared paths normalize slash runs/trailing separators without resolving or opening paths.
Selector fixtures exercise dispatch conditions only; complete result/error/default wire fixtures remain required.

reservation-boundary.json pins full fresh top-level and nested reservation field sets for all eleven variants and both aliases; public API tests compare these sets and semantic values, rather than only selecting a branch.

Current canonical action normalization, finite lease defaults/bounds, path separator deduplication, absent/null distinctions, text-container refusal, privacy projections, rollback and keyed receipt shapes are executable boundary fixtures.
Scalar coercion is asymmetric: candidate is an API text key but base/resource/item/successor are helper-normalized. Equal helper meaning is not automatically equal keyed fingerprint.

Malformed acquire arguments are fixtured at the public door (tests/test_state_reservation_boundary.py): lease_s/stale_s go straight to float(), so non-numeric text or a container is an unhandled 500, and 'nan' lease_s is a 500 raised later. inf, negative, '0' and >MAX values refuse 422 'lease_s and stale_s must be positive and bounded'. A falsy 0 falls back to the default lease, True reads as 1.0, and '1e3' is accepted.

Recorded legacy defects, not approved native behaviour: stale_s='nan' passes the bound check and is committed as NaN; resource and path entries that are containers or numbers are stringified ('[1]', "{'a': 1}", '123'); an empty item acquires an item-less reservation; container or numeric item values refuse as 'reservation is not visible to this collaborator'.

Only action and candidate pass through the shared _norm_args text normalisation (a container refuses 422 '<field> must be text, not <type>'). resource/item/base/successor/reservation/paths/lease_s/stale_s reach the helper raw. Refusals that commit nothing keep the {'detail': str} shape.
An unhandled exception is serialized as HTTP 500 {'detail': '<Type>: <message>', 'error': {type, message, path, method, unhandled: true}}, echoing the exception text; nothing is committed.

Shared-wrapper refusals are fixtured. 401 'missing authentication; …' and 401 'agent credential is invalid or expired; …' come from engine/launch.py's authentication middleware, which is outside the pinned backend module set, so they carry no source span. 403 'agent credential identity mismatch' also covers an org the credential does not belong to. 409 halt and killswitch refuse before the lock. Request-schema errors are FastAPI 422 with a LIST-shaped detail ({type, loc, msg, input}) for a non-object args, a missing field or invalid JSON. Unknown top-level request fields are ignored.

facts: This specifies the current legacy reservation receipt contract. Native original-key custody/exact-result retention and runtime proof remain separate unqualified v6 work; no current receipt is represented as a complete saved response.

Both aliases and every action are transaction+post. A bare unkeyed call files no operation receipt. A keyed call must use orgtree_op_call with inner tool/args/key/epoch; envelope key fields, missing epoch, and nested receipt verbs refuse before dispatch.

Admission occurs within write_org, after caller existence/halt/killswitch checks but before reservation predicates. A retained same-key replay therefore bypasses current reservation state/item predicates. Current authentication still runs before this point; native disclosure revalidation is not claimed to exist in this legacy branch.

Fingerprint is full SHA256 of canonical tool/node/generation/normalized args. Tool aliases are distinct identities. Admission normalizes only the API text-key set first; the helper later strips/lowers action, so action spelling variants can select the same domain operation yet conflict under one key.

Admission checks key syntax, custody epoch and key age before looking for a retained row. A retained different fingerprint conflicts; a matching fence or foreign generation refuses; otherwise the row replays. Only an absent row reaches the newer-schema and eviction-watermark refusals. Receipts are found across generations and classified at their original generation and fingerprint subject.

Accepted replay returns exactly replayed/op_id/at/tool/outcome/receipt/status, not the original result and not a second helper call, save or wake. It does not repeat a post-commit effect whose prior outcome is unknown.

Immediately before save, the API appends an applied receipt in the same org transaction as reservation state and any release mail/audience changes. Refusal or a pre-commit save exception leaves none durable. The process sequence witness advances after save while the lock remains held.

The stored result is a scalar allowlist plus restricted reservation/overlap rows, capped at 128 list entries; created/updated/heartbeat timestamps, stale reasons, contention view tags and arbitrary data are omitted. Landing-query rows and stale-ID lists are not retained; count may describe more rows than the slice stores.

Post-effects list drive for this receipt class and observed is the literal unknown, even for domain-read actions. Release carrier delivery is added only after filing and saving, so it is absent from the receipt result.

Receipt schema/coverage are 1; keys permit 60-second future skew. More than 500 rows trim to 400 and raise from_ms strictly beyond the greatest evicted mint, never lower it. Retained matching rows can replay even below this watermark while epoch/age/generation checks hold; the watermark guards admission only when the row is absent.

Lookup classifies a retained row before answering. A current-epoch absent eligible reservation key is durably fenced and returns not_applied; its delayed original refuses. Under an old epoch, a matching applied row is positive evidence, but an absent row is unknown and no new fence is written. No lookup/custody classification permits executing an absent old key after uncertain restore.
This reservation helper only mutates its supplied document; no filesystem/process/network action is executed.
Outer dispatch receipt/diagnostic contacts are a separate unresolved obligation.

Release with a successor requires the successor to be live and able to read the reservation's nonempty item; otherwise reservations.execute refuses 'successor is not a live collaborator' before any mail. An archived successor is therefore refused, so this path never reaches post_mail's deferred (non-live recipient) branch.

On a first release the api adapter calls Org.post_mail(actor, successor, body, 'status') inside the same store.write_org/DOC_LOCK cycle as the reservation transition. post_mail's addressing check (downward any depth, one hop up, sibling, or held audience) runs there, and its refusal discards the whole release, including the reservation transition.

post_mail writes into the uncommitted document: one untyped status row (from=actor, kind=status, body 'Reservation <id> was released; its release receipt is <receipt>.', relationship, message_id=id, operation_id, recv_seq with seq_origin=deposit and the mailbox identity) through deposit_mail, which also mirrors the row into mail_log and advances only the recipient node's mail_seq; one events row op=mail carrying post_mail's warnings; and one lifecycle row state=accepted, delivery=mailbox.

A reply-audience grant (grantee=successor, grantor=actor, reason '<actor> messaged directly') is appended only when the actor is a strict ancestor but not the parent of the successor, and no audience already exists. Siblings, direct reports and repeat releases add none. post_mail's warnings reach the event log, not the tool result.

mail_notify(org, actor, successor) runs before the save as a UI hint, so it fires even when the save then fails. After the save, exactly one supervisor.send_message(org, successor, ping, mail_ping=True, sender=actor, ping_reason='agent_mail') runs, and its carrier note becomes result.delivery.

The ping's delivery outcome is not observed: the receipt records post_effects expected=['drive'], observed='unknown'. A failure after the commit leaves the release, mail and grant durable, and a keyed retry replays the receipt without re-driving. A RELEASED replay returns notified:null and posts nothing.

Physical storage contacts of these writes belong to the unresolved `contacts` instrumentation facet (P02). What send_message does after it is invoked is runtime delivery (P08), outside this contract. Pinned by tests/test_state_reservation_boundary.py (release notification, reply grant, precommit/postcommit failure and addressing-refusal cases).
Declare domain changes separately from actual database/connection/receipt/log/effect contacts.
A pre-storage refusal must record zero contacts; a whole-operation claim needs every causal continuation.

It was re-run independently, and every observed fact below is asserted by tests/test_state_p02_contact_facets.py, which runs the same probe.

Per variant (all 11, under both aliases, cold and warm), a call has exactly one attributed census record, and its statement count equals the harness's SQL-level count. There are 0 unbound statements. Only the primary org store is touched: no sidecar store, no foreign org store, no process or network contact, and no isolation-guard refusal. Cold calls read doc, log_d, log_l, meta and nodes with one new connection; warm calls read doc, meta and nodes on pooled connections. list-read, landing and overlap write nothing; list-scope, acquire, renew, recover, invalidate, release and land write doc; release-notify writes doc, log_d, log_l and nodes. Every write falls inside an explicit transaction on the autocommit primary store.

Callback probes: supervisor.send_message and api.mail_notify are spies, counted and never delivered. release-notify calls each exactly once; no other variant calls either. Cold calls also repeat the os.mkdir(exist_ok) of the orgs directory (store._orgs_dir), a filesystem contact with no durable change.

Refusals and keyed paths have bounded contacts. 401 (token gate): no record, 0 statements. 403: 0 statements. The 409 halt/killswitch before the lock, the 422 unaddressable successor, the 422 retained-row cap, the 409 keyed conflict, the 422 stale epoch and a keyed replay all read but write nothing and wake nobody. A fresh keyed call writes its receipt (doc, log_l, meta) inside a transaction.

Hidden-contact negative control: control:hidden-contact (a statement on a pooled connection through a plain cursor) is seen as census hidden_steps >= 1, and every other reservation row shows 0. A separate ORG-STORE control, control:foreign-org-contact, is classified org-db:foreign, and no other reservation row touches a foreign org store. That control is org-store locality only; agent-level mail locality is the next fact.

Agent-level mail-locality negative control (the clause S2b ruling R1 left open). Each row's P02 `agents` block reads which agents an operation touched in two layers. Logical: the org's mail, mail_log, notices, delivering and audiences before and after the call. Physical: node ids in the statement parameters of agent-keyed rows (nodes, log_d). In all four release-notify rows (both aliases, cold and warm), every changed mail and mail_log entry, and every physically written agent row, belongs to the named successor alone (role target). The sender's own entries never change, so the contacts are never self-only, and no third agent is touched. The negative control control:third-agent-mail (a release whose notify step also posts to a third agent) is flagged both logically and physically (third_agent_mail >= 1, third_agent_rows_written >= 1). No other reservation row touches a third agent, and only release-notify produces mail.

The same holds for a successor reachable only through an audience the user granted to the sender (P02 row audience-successor:reservation.release-notify, v3 0679103, S2c finding f1): its mail and mail_log changes and its physical node row belong to that successor alone, and no third agent is touched. Asserted by tests/test_state_p02_contact_facets.py.

Limit of that control: the legacy mail QUEUE, notices, delivering and audiences are each one org-wide doc row, so a queue write is physically a rewrite of that org-wide row. The agent-level result rests on the logical before/after reading of that row plus the per-agent nodes and log_d rows. Per-agent physical stores are a P04 native design question, outside this legacy facet.

Loss accounting. For the window, rejected, dropped_stale_window, dropped_capture_off, evicted, db_late, db_observe_failed, db_self_recursion and db_hidden_unattributed are all 0. Each row's own counter deltas bracket its single request and contain only observed/recorded/skipped_self/unclassified_action (db_unattributed and db_late deltas 0, statements_unbound 0). The window-level db_unattributed is harness fixture work between operations, not attributed to any operation.

This facet specifies legacy read-material authorization, not native Effective fencing. Both tools call the same _agent_read_access before reading content; shared middleware/transport and operator/bridge paths remain separately unresolved.

The public agent path authenticates org/node/generation, requires a live unreplaced caller, and checks halt/killswitch before these reads. The tool-specific read then obtains a seq-guarded cached org, without a document transaction around content production.

Self wins first; strict descendant ancestry wins second, even for an archived target. Otherwise the shared-item route checks the active work_items collection, current holder/reviewer/participant standing, and the target node name in the holder roster except its last row. Creator, org visibility and unrelated-item membership do not independently grant material access.

The item access disclosure includes via,item,title,standing,held_from,derived,note. Stored holder rows survive history folding. An absent roster is derived from surviving assign history/current owner without persisting it.

Once a route authorizes the target, the adapter exposes that target scratch namespace or bounded transcript; it does not filter returned content by work-item tags. The item is an authorization witness, not a content selector. Any finer native content policy requires an explicit design/product ruling.

Legacy limits must remain visible: work_items is a storage-placement test, not status!=done; a done item still in that collection can grant until archive. A returning current holder also appearing earlier in its roster can match. _work_actor_node extracts the node string without checking born or generation, despite roster rows carrying born. These are source observations, not approved native permissions.

Membership is recomputed for the next call after a saved removal/archive. The legacy implementation does not revalidate while file/transcript content is being produced, and does not acquire an output claim. A successful initial check therefore is not proof that a later restriction became Effective safely.

Read predicates are authenticated caller liveness/generation and runtime halt state; self identity or the target parent chain; otherwise active item membership, current role, and previous roster membership. Content is reached only after _agent_read_access returns.

Legacy item matching searches active items in stored order and takes the latest matching target in each prior roster. The first granting item supplies the disclosure; full-org active-item scans are existing cost, not a native query plan.

The native contract must close authorization with the disclosed output and immutable identity using the approved affected-consumer fence. No source-bound assertion here authorizes a global read lock or repeats legacy name-only/returning-holder holes.

Both tools are classified NONE and return before the public document receipt admission/save path. An accepted orgtree_op_call envelope is unwrapped but these reads file no applied receipt, perform no original-key replay, and reevaluate authority/content on every retry.

The wrapper still refuses envelope op_key/op_epoch, missing inner key/args, missing epoch and nested receipt verbs. A present read key is not admitted against epoch/key syntax by these early-return branches. A current-epoch lookup without an applied receipt reports unknown/unsupported_operation and creates no fence.
No-receipt is not no-write: filesystem creation and transcript/reply sidecar writes can occur. Idempotency, current-disclosure and native/Rust conformance remain subject to their own gates.

The read door consults cached org snapshots for caller/halt/target/item/ancestry. Scratch resolves an OS realpath beneath the shared lineage scratch root, checks isdir/isfile, enumerates the whole directory before a 200-name slice, or reads the whole UTF-8 replacement-decoded file before a 20000-character slice.

scratch_dir additionally checks disk placement through sandbox.on_disk (which can load org state) and can reload org data on directory creation. Disk-backed UNC resolution, sandbox ownership, storage-pool/cache misses and every transitive helper are not an exhaustive contact map yet.

read_chat calls chat_window.read_window and unique_cards. The current transcript stack consults provider files, prompt/import sidecars, retained transcript records, projection cache, assistant state, runtime state and reply snapshots. The bounded fixture witnesses three SQLite surfaces; it does not enumerate every provider/import/sandbox branch.

Disk-backed (sandbox:on-disk, scratch and transcript), the path is resolved through wsl, which the probe's isolation guard refuses, so the read fails with a 500 before any file is read: the disk-backed read contacts are NOT observed. Recorded from P02's source reading, not run: where Docker Desktop's WSL distro is down or absent, disk.distro() raises DiskError, which the agent read path does not catch (it catches LedgerError), so the caller gets a 500 carrying DiskError's text rather than a refusal; whether that should be a clean refusal is a product question, not decided here (docket item disk-backed-sandbox-reads-return-a-raw-500-when). facts: The early API branch has no explicit org save or operation receipt, but a cold transcript helper mints reply/transcript incarnation identifiers under DOC_LOCK and saves the org. The shared snapshot is not stamped, so the same call can repeat reply-incarnation save cycles before the next fresh snapshot. Warm pre-minted fixture reads avoid these org saves; neither case files an operation receipt.

scratch_dir creates a missing lineage directory and attempts sandbox ownership repair, with exceptions swallowed. No atomic transaction couples that directory or ownership attempt to the earlier read authorization.

Transcript reads can initialize/write transcript-records.sqlite3, chat-window-index.sqlite3 and reply-events.sqlite3 in separate SQLite connections and transactions, independently of the cold org identity saves. Ingestion/retained quote data is not automatically disposable projection data. Runtime caches can also change.
open_questions: Complete physical write/effect coverage and native placement for every transitive branch; no cross-database atomicity has been established.

Owner: native placement at P04 (schema/sidecar). Closes with: a native placement decision for the transcript-records, chat-window-index and reply-events writes. facts: No org-wide DOC_LOCK spans these tools from authority to response. Cold identity mints do individually take DOC_LOCK and save; snapshot publication, transcript SQLite transactions and runtime locks have their own boundaries. Those boundaries do not make authorization plus disclosure atomic.

Plain transcript calls wait on a four-reader per-event-loop limiter before executing their fresh agent identity/state checks. The legacy route recognizes the plain tool name; an OP_CALL-wrapped read uses the general worker path. Neither path grants a durable output fence.
Native conversion must use the approved narrow authorization/output protocol, current immutable identities and bounded indexed item lookups, and must prove disjoint reads/writers remain independent.

facts: The local tool adapter shapes are executable in material-read-boundary.json and tests/test_state_material_reads.py. Scratch returns dir/access/entries, file/access/content, or error/access (missing path is HTTP200); path escape and text-container errors are HTTP422 detail. OS errors are not converted to missing-path success.

Transcript returns node,busy,access,occupancy,occupancy_estimated,messages. Each projected message retains only role,text,tools, truncates text to 1200 characters, defaults absent tools to [], and preserves an explicit tools:null. The outer last slice remains even when read_chat supplies extra rows.

last defaults to30 for missing/null/empty, coerces through int then float-to-int, and clamps to1..80; malformed or nonfinite values return422. node/path use shared text normalization: null restores default, scalars stringify, containers refuse. The card schema is stricter than the gateway coercion.

The scratch path is stripped, leading separators removed, then realpath-resolved with a separator-anchored containment check. Its 20000/200/1200 bounds constrain returned characters or entries, not underlying IO or all nested response bytes.

Door parity is fixtured in tests/test_state_reservation_boundary.py::test_every_p01_tool_shares_the_agent_operator_and_bridge_door_shapes for all five non-reservation P01 tools. Agent credential: 401 missing or invalid, 403 identity mismatch. The desktop operator token acts as any live node, and as node=user gets 403 'authenticated seat is missing; …'. Request-schema errors are FastAPI 422 with a list-shaped detail. Halt/killswitch is 409 before the lock. An unhandled error uses the shared 500 serializer, whose body echoes the exception text (see wire-common).

BridgeGateway: a valid org bridge secret may call /api/agent as ANY node of that org, with or without an agent credential. Another org gets 403 'bridge secret is scoped to its own org'; an unknown secret gets 403 'forbidden'. Only the standalone api.main starts BridgeGateway; the desktop launch path engine/launch.py never does. This is recorded, not approved; docket item p05-authority-review-bridge-org-secret-acts-as-a owns the decision.

The legacy transcript projector (supervisor._read_chat_source, through chat_window.read_window and supervisor.read_chat) is fixtured at the public orgtree_read_transcript door, one fresh org per row type, in tests/test_state_material_reads.py (TranscriptProjector). An agent receives only role, text (cut to 1200 characters) and tools; every other projected field (thinking, codexPlan, cmd_out, summary, segments, native ids) never reaches it.

Rows that project to nothing: unparseable lines, JSON that is not an object, isSidechain/isMeta records, system subtypes other than compact_boundary/api_error/local_command, record types other than user/assistant/system/codex_plan_updated, a non-object message, isVisibleInTranscriptOnly, 'No response requested.', a compact summary (attached to its boundary, invisible to agents), pure tool_result plumbing, and an empty transcript.

Rows that project to text: assistant string content and joined non-blank text blocks; user string content or its first text block (an image block beside it is dropped, and an image-only prompt projects nothing); a slash-command echo as '/<name> <args>'; a compact boundary as '— context compacted —' with ' · N.Nk tokens' when preTokens is numeric; api_error as '⚠ API error — ' plus 300 characters; a <synthetic> model or isApiErrorMessage as '⚠ ' plus 300 characters, speaking as system.

Rows that project to EMPTY text because their payload is invisible to agents: codex_plan_updated (assistant); thinking with or without text, including Codex journal thinking (signature 'codex') (assistant; two thinking records of one message merge into one row); local_command output and old-CLI <local-command-stdout> (system); and an assistant record with no content.

Tool chips reach the agent whole: name, arg, id, and, once its tool_result arrives, result (first 60 lines, capped at 2000 characters), result_lines, truncated, error, images, TodoWrite glyphs, diff from structuredPatch, task totals, and file/mail/work/presentation links recognised from both bare and mcp__orgtree__-prefixed names. Every chip also carries reply-target fields (event_id 'reply_…', reply_quote and, with a result, result_event_id/result_reply_quote).

Merged rows: steered_log entries appear as user rows and steer misses as '— <text> —' system rows, turn_error_log entries as '⚠ <text>' system rows, all interleaved by timestamp; a preserving bearer's oracle exchanges follow as user/assistant pairs.

Recorded legacy disclosure: a user event carrying orgtree's own envelope ([ORG STATE …]) with no prompt-view sidecar row is rendered RAW to the reader (D-229 fail-open, since the adapter reads with hold_back=False), so a reader sees the author's machine envelope. With a view row, only its visible text is shown. A machine-only view hides the row, UNLESS the view's segments carry a human-visible wake card (a state/drive segment whose event variant is human-visible, for example reminder.working_checkup), which keeps an empty-text user row.

Recorded legacy defects: a content list holding a non-object block (AttributeError) or non-iterable content such as a number (TypeError) fails the WHOLE read with the shared 500 serializer, although record-level and message-level malformations are skipped.

Legacy records with no provider id (no uuid, no message.id) are all projected. Byte-identical twins stay two rows, and each row's tool chips carry distinct reply event_ids (no aliasing of one reply target).

Codex/Antigravity journal shapes: the P08b provider-echo marker (top-level orgtree_origin on a tool_result record) is ignored by the projector, so the chip gets its result and links as usual. A late tool result journaled by supervisor._late_tool_result under an id no tool_use carries (codex-late-N) matches no chip and projects nothing.

facts: Legacy source contract for structural inspection and capability reporting only. The real agent HTTP door authenticates the org/node/generation, refuses archived/replaced callers and halt/killswitch, then these branches load an independent org and require the named caller live. Frozen-profile middleware additionally rejects non-loopback non-bridge clients before the diagnostic. Neither branch adds an operator identity or grants a permission.

Inspection visibility is self; team (self plus siblings sharing the same parent, not the parent or children); subtree (self plus recursive descendants); or full (rooted tree). The helper falls back to team for an empty value, but Org construction backfills a missing visibility with full before the public branch runs. These legacy defaults are distinct. Explicit hidden or unknown targets refuse as one whole request before any _safe_node call. Item membership and material-read audience grants do not broaden this structural visibility.

include_archived controls the visible universe as well as explicit target eligibility. Live-only output finally filters state exactly equal to live. The selected node row may still carry its parent id even when the parent row itself is outside visibility; that existing structural reference is not authority to inspect the parent.

Capability operations are the install-wide available_tools catalogue, not a filtered list of actions authorized for this actor/target. Restricted scope is displayed separately. Subsequent real dispatch repeats its ordinary authority checks.

Legacy deficiencies remain explicit: an unrecognized nonempty visibility falls through to full, and current generation/visibility is not fenced through completed output. The native design must not adopt these as acceptable default authority.

Caller liveness/generation and halt state; current visibility; current parent edges, child ordering and archive states define structural eligibility. Explicit targets intersect the computed visible set and retain request order and duplicates. Empty targets, including a list containing only empty strings, mean all visible rows.

A node grant/free projection also reads its current tier price and immediate non-archived children grants and prices; those children may be outside the requested output. Returned free is not a one-row read or a promise of spend authority. Archived rows return free:null.

Legacy children scans all node rows without an index argument, descendants recursively invokes it, and ordinary load_org materializes all eager nodes even for one target. Those costs are obligations for indexed native reads, never native acceptance criteria.

Neither diagnostic is present in the current legacy coverage table: coverage returns the empty unknown string, not the explicit NONE class. Their early dispatch branches nevertheless return before receipt admission/save. This classifier gap is recorded, not silently relabeled.

A syntactically accepted OP_CALL unwrap executes these reads freshly on each retry; no applied receipt is recorded, no duplicate is replayed and an unsupported-operation lookup cannot fence the key. Missing required wrapper data/nested wrappers still refuse. No fresh-operation namespace or native replay policy is inferred from that omission.

Agent authentication and halt checks use cached_org; the diagnostic branch separately calls load_org. For SQLite, _load_sqlite_org takes pooled connections and _load_lazy reads eager doc and all nodes in a short BEGIN/COMMIT snapshot before projecting. Unnamed lazy sections, if reached, can observe a later revision.

Inspection reads structural/operational node fields, tier prices and child grant totals; provider_of uses static membership/prefix checks. Capabilities reads the MCP cards plus deployment profile and desktop-managed environment selectors. Ordinary capability reporting does not probe provider CLIs or network services.

The SQL fixture attaches to actual pooled acquisitions and retains only statement verbs, recognized table labels and a boolean for the known all-node SELECT. It distinguishes output size from underlying materialization without retaining SQL values.

Observed by the P02 per-operation probe (tools/p02_operation_contacts.py; docs/state-system/p02-operation-contacts.md) (v3 0679103, synthetic), answering both questions above. Middleware and schema/pool cold-path reads on SQLite were observed earlier (b6568a1); legacy input is the migration rows (diagnostic.writes).

JSON store backend (json:* rows): inspect and capabilities answer 200 cold and warm without any SQL statement; each reads the org's own JSON document (store._read_bytes, class data:org-db:own), and the cold call also reads code files (lazy imports). The killswitch refusal answers 409 after reading the document. No row has an unknown contact.

Malformed stored state: 18 corruptions of one node field, each with that node as the named target (:node) and as a bystander in an all-visible inspection (:org), on BOTH backends (72 rows). The HTTP outcome is identical on the two backends: 500 for generation "x" or [1], grant "x" or null, model 5 or null, scope "bad" and scope.tools "bad" (either role); 422 for parent "ghost" and state "weird" only when the corrupt node is the named target (200 as a bystander); 200 for the rest. JSON rows run no statement. The whole-org 500 is the recorded diagnostic.wire defect.
Limits carried from P02: synthetic data, statements and file contacts only (no rows examined, pages or lock waits). Asserted by tests/test_state_p02_contact_facets.py.

These two leaf adapters do not call save_org or mutate the document. An already-created/migrated SQLite fixture proves no domain save, DML or org-sequence change during its measured read window. Volatile caches/probe state are outside that domain assertion.

Do not turn this into a universal no-write claim: load_org calls _ensure_migrated, which can finish an interrupted migration or invoke migrate_org for legacy JSON under the existing ownership gate. Pool/schema initialization, caches and request diagnostics also require separate accounting. This package never runs a migration or startup lifecycle.
Observed by the P02 per-operation probe (tools/p02_operation_contacts.py; docs/state-system/p02-operation-contacts.md) (v3 0679103), answering both questions above, on the migration paths:

migration:legacy-json (a legacy .json org under the SQLite backend with ORGTREE_MIGRATE): the cold read migrates inside the call. It reads the JSON document, writes doc, log_d, log_l, meta and nodes, renames the document aside (os.rename in migrate_org) and removes stale database files (os.remove in _remove_db_files), then answers 200. The warm repeat writes nothing.

migration:interrupted: store._finish_interrupted_migration completes a half-done migration with one rename and no statement write, then answers 200. migration:refused (no ORGTREE_MIGRATE): 500 MigrationRefused, 0 statements, nothing written. migration:malformed-json: 500 MigrationError after reading the bad document, nothing written.

Cold-schema: the only file mutation outside the org store on any cold diagnostic row is the orgs-directory os.mkdir(exist_ok) in store._orgs_dir. Request-diagnostic writes: the slow-request trace (reservation wrapper-writes) is the one durable one and fires only past its threshold, which these synthetic rows do not reach. Cache writes are process memory. Asserted by tests/test_state_p02_contact_facets.py.

The ordinary diagnostic leaf loads outside DOC_LOCK and holds no single transaction from identity check through output. _load_lazy protects its eager snapshot, not the preceding authenticated-generation check or later disclosure. Cache/pool/SQLite admission may impose separate waits.

A narrowed inspection still computes full visibility and free amounts. Native execution must read the actual affected topology/visibility/generation/archive/catalog/child facts with the approved output claim/fence; it must not add an org-wide visibility/version lock to replace these scans.

The legacy controlled race fixtures mutate only disposable state between defined source boundaries. They show stale-generation and restriction-during-projection windows; they are not native concurrency success tests.

facts: The fixture pins the local structural fields and nested allowlists, role/visibility metadata, request order/duplicates, archived filtering and selected malformed argument refusals. Private account identity becomes present/missing/provider facts; charter, session, mail, transcript, directories and status summaries are omitted.

nodes must be a list when supplied; each element is then stringified, empty strings removed by inspect_state, and all targets checked together. nodes takes precedence over node even when empty. node uses shared text normalization. include_archived uses shared string-aware flag semantics, not plain bool of a string.

Capabilities returns actor,surface,operations,operator_only,agent_only,scope. The catalogue follows standard/frozen policy and desktop alias replacement, preserves order and has no provider availability guarantee. Topology/operator metadata cannot elevate the caller.

Allowed operational field values are projected as currently stored with selected bool/int/string coercions; this is an allowlist of fields, not recursive secret sanitization or a byte limit. Restored/malformed field types and complete middleware/error/Rust parity remain unresolved.

Malformed stored node fields are fixtured in tests/test_state_diagnostic_boundary.py (test_malformed_stored_node_fields_pin_legacy_projection_or_failure). A non-integer generation, a non-numeric or null grant, a model outside the tier catalogue, or a non-dict scope/tools raises while the inspection is built, and the whole call is a 500. The same happens for an UNFILTERED inspection of the whole org, so one corrupt node denies the diagnostic to every caller whose visible set includes it.

An unknown state value or a dangling parent drops the node from the visible set (422 'state inspection is outside your visible scope' when targeted, silently absent from the whole org). A malformed frozen/pending_switch/last_status map projects as null. A null generation projects as 0; a negative grant, a non-string org_visibility and a numeric title are projected as stored.

facts: Normal diagnostic leaves do not intentionally send mail, wake/launch a process, inspect a transcript or change provider/account credentials. available_tools only evaluates deployment environment and transforms local card definitions.

Transitive storage acquisition can encounter migration/recovery guards before the nominal read. Request profiling and in-memory caching are separate effects. The measured diagnostic fixture directly blocks process launches, domain saves and transcript reads. Provider-network absence is source-inspection evidence, not a universal executable network prohibition.

Observed by the P02 per-operation probe (tools/p02_operation_contacts.py; docs/state-system/p02-operation-contacts.md) (v3 0679103), answering both questions above. Failure semantics on the legacy and recovery paths: refused migration gives 500 MigrationRefused with the operator's guidance, and nothing is written; a malformed legacy document gives 500 MigrationError naming the file, and nothing is written; a legacy document with ORGTREE_MIGRATE is migrated inside the read and then served; an interrupted migration is finished by _ensure_migrated (one rename) and then served.
No diagnostic row, on either backend, cold or warm, has a process, network or provider contact, or any guard refusal. Asserted by tests/test_state_p02_contact_facets.py.
P01 records source-backed predicates and fixture-only actual pooled SQL contacts. No production logger is enabled and no live data, statement values or credentials are recorded by the test observer.

P01's own fixture tests do not supply the logical-operation denominator, the actual physical/logical contacts or the loss accounting; P02's per-operation record (below) does, on synthetic data. These tests do not measure latency, CPU/GIL capacity or native storage concurrency.

Observed by the P02 per-operation probe (tools/p02_operation_contacts.py; docs/state-system/p02-operation-contacts.md) (synthetic data, v3 be8a05e): a drift-aware contact/profile/loss record for both tools. Every diagnostic row (inspect and capabilities; the SQLite and JSON backends; malformed stored state; the migration paths; cold and warm) carries one census record matching the harness, a profile, zero per-row loss and no unknown contact, and the probe refuses any contact a row does not declare (its drift refusal). The profile has total time on every row, and handler and unattributed time on every row the handler answered; the 34 rows that failed with a 500 (malformed stored state on either backend, and the refused and malformed-JSON migrations) carry only total time and the stages they reached (the org load, or the migration's lock and mutate stages). P02's hand-off records this probe-level record as reviewed with its candidate and leaves to P01 whether that meets the clause; the coordinator ruled (2026-09-24 21:14Z) that it does. It approves the probe, not a product drift policy, and runtime_census stays false. Native negative controls are the P03 gate, not a clause of this legacy facet (S2d decision 1, reviewer ruling on 803227e). Asserted by tests/test_state_p02_contact_facets.py.

This contract covers the authenticated orgtree_preview tool only. Existing agent authentication/generation/halt admission still runs; its separate leaf load requires the caller live. The actor is the authenticated seat, never a nested actor argument. The operator /ops preview surface is explicitly separate and remains a pending registration.

The public agent allowlist has thirteen spellings, including three pairs of aliases. One leading orgtree_ prefix is removed, with no case folding or whitespace trim. Agent move batches use operation=move with moves; the helper-only move_batch spelling and operator-only delete/rescind/reseed/promote/demote remain refused at this door.

The detached Org executes the ordinary ledger authority checks: management reach, self restrictions, grant ceilings, topology and capability checks are not bypassed by preview. Structural visibility is not management authority. The matrix exercises each admitted spelling and selected refusals; this does not claim all underlying transition predicates are fully specified.

Retool/set_scope account selection is checked before the shadow: never self, descendants only, validate_selection against the current target model. Directory translation also occurs before cloning. Switch previews run provider_hire_gate, check_switch_account and a live supervisor busy lookup before the ledger simulation. Those are real read/preflight adapters, not guaranteed pure in-memory calls.

The ordinary operator preview path has its own allowlist and DOC_LOCK scope; it does not expose agent-only topology operations. Selected HTTP authentication/refusal tests keep these surfaces distinct, without declaring the entire operator route covered.

Legacy orgtree_preview is absent from the receipt coverage table: coverage is empty unknown, not explicit NONE. Its early branch returns before receipt admission or save. Syntactically accepted receipt wrappers therefore simulate freshly; a supported-wrapper lookup for this tool reports unknown/unsupported and cannot fence the key.

A preview response applied:false is a simulation result, not a durable acceptance, reservation or future execution token. Repeating it after a real state change recomputes from current loaded state; it neither reserves credit nor executes the future operation.

inspect_state projects before and after visibility over nodes and funding dependencies. isolated() JSON-serializes the entire Org document before constructing the shadow. On a LazyDoc this traverses items()/materialize_all and owner maps, so a narrow preview can read unrelated retained mail/history as well as every eager node.

The source-bound fixture observes actual pooled SQLite acquisitions and selected lazy-section materialization labels on disposable, already-migrated data. It retains no SQL values or payloads. Whole-document traversal and hidden sections are source/fixture evidence, not a measured clone-byte budget or a proposed native read strategy.

The eager SQLite snapshot does not make all separately loaded lazy sections or provider/registry/runtime observations one consistent transaction. Before projection and the isolated clone are sequential reads; pending native snapshot and output-fence requirements remain.

Native design r7 (docket design-the-native-conflict-predicate-and-isolati artifact r7, sha256 24e86a19f95b47ef2a2acabfbc8d8f4861268f555692167ea019c9c80f160792; approved by review artifact r10, sha256 8be9323173dd1ae785f66328a8481a12bf86c7f2c816797c1c9c496c01ea895b): section 6.2 and C6 are the approved bounded native simulation this facet's clause asks for. Admission is as legacy (the thirteen spellings); external observations (provider availability and authentication, the credential service, sandbox path mapping) are observed first and traced, not claimed consistent with the snapshot; one REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY snapshot reads the caller's identity, generation and visibility, the before projection and the transition's declared read set (section 6.4); decide is pure; the after projection is computed in memory. No whole-document clone, and no read of mail bodies, transcripts, docket history or events. The clause asks for the approved design only, so the facet is specified; qualification (Q-P1) runs at P03 for reallocate and at P05 for the rest (D11), and completing the observed provider-preflight contacts stays with P02 and P08 (r7 section 6.6).

The leaf calls ordinary mutators on a JSON-detached Org, then drops it. Domain changes, queued model records, event logs, mail, audiences and warnings generated in that shadow are not persisted by the preview branch. The public agent default include_archived is True, evaluated with plain bool; a nonempty string such as false is truthy and explicit null is false. This intentionally records the legacy mismatch with state inspection string-aware flags and the pure helper default False.

Falsy nested args become an empty object before type checking; truthy non-dicts refuse. Nested text fields use _norm_args. Unknown retool fields are ignored by its whitelist, including account after prevalidation; nested actor does not change the caller.

Selected malformed numeric inputs reach legacy 500 errors. The isolated simulation may otherwise report success without a visible diff (for example hidden charter/directory/account state). Neither result shape nor empty diff proves no hypothetical change.

Per-operation malformed arguments are fixtured in tests/test_state_preview_boundary.py (test_per_operation_malformed_arguments_pin_legacy_refusals) for reallocate, move, swap, self_subjugate, retool, retire, dissolve, revoke_dir, switch_model and audience. facts: The agent HTTP door authenticates before this branch: _agent_identity refuses a credential for another org/node, a missing seat, an archived or replaced seat, a stale generation and a seat_id mismatch (all 403), reading the shared cached_org snapshot. A missing or invalid token is refused 401 by engine/launch.py's middleware, outside the pinned backend set.

Halt and killswitch refuse 409 twice: supervisor.halt.blocked before the write cycle, and again under the write cycle from the caller's own node row and the org killswitch. Pinned: a halted caller gets 409 and nothing commits.

The operation is self-only. No argument names a target: an extra `node` argument is ignored and the report is written to the caller's own node row. The only other agent it can touch is the caller's stored parent, as the recipient of a done/blocked report.

The report mail to the parent goes through Org.post_mail as kind=status from the caller; the parent is the caller's superior, so no audience grant is needed or created (pinned: audiences unchanged). A top-level caller (parent null) posts no mail.

`status` and `summary` pass through _norm_args: a container refuses 422 '<field> must be text, not <type>'; an explicit null is dropped so the defaults apply (status 'working', summary ''); a bare number becomes its text.

The status VALUE IS NOT VALIDATED server-side. The MCP card's enum (working, done, blocked, idle) is a client schema only: any other text, including '', 'bogus', '5' and 'DONE', is stored verbatim as last_status.status and answered as recorded. Recorded legacy behaviour, not approved native behaviour.
Exactly 'done' is stored as 'idle' (user ruling 2026-08-02) but answered as recorded 'done'. Exactly 'working' sets working_activity_at to the report time; every other value pops it.
Mail is posted only for exactly 'done' or 'blocked' (case-sensitive) when the caller has a parent. 'DONE' records and mails nothing.
The summary has no length cap: a 100000-character summary is stored whole on the node and, for done/blocked, in the mail body. Recorded legacy behaviour.

TX_POST: the call runs in the resident write cycle (store.write_org under DOC_LOCK) and ends in save_org for every accepted report. Measured with the committed document read cold (resident evicted), by outcome:
working/idle/any non-reporting value, or done/blocked from a top-level caller: only the caller's node row changes (last_status {status, summary, at}; working_activity_at set or removed).

done/blocked with a parent: the caller's node row, plus one status mail in the parent's mailbox (body '[DONE] <summary>' or '[BLOCKED] <summary>', typed ev status.report with state and summary), one mail_log row, one 'mail' event, one accepted lifecycle row (delivery mailbox), and the parent's mail_seq (and mailbox_id on its first mail). No audience row.
A keyed call adds op_receipts and op_receipts_meta in the same save. A keyed replay and every refusal (422 container, 409 halt, 403 archived) commit nothing.
This is the same wrapper as the reservation family's wrapper-writes; physical SQL statements, row fan-out and waits behind these section changes belong to status.instrumentation (P02).

Source read set: the door reads the cached_org snapshot for caller identity/generation/seat; the write cycle reads the resident document for the caller's node, halt and the org killswitch; a report reads the caller's parent and Org.post_mail's mailbox/addressing state for that parent; a keyed call reads the receipts sections.

Observed by the P02 per-operation probe (tools/p02_operation_contacts.py; docs/state-system/p02-operation-contacts.md) (v3 3a2ec7b, SQLite) for every outcome, cold and warm. Warm: a report that posts no mail (working, idle, an unvalidated value, done or blocked at top level) reads only meta and nodes; done or blocked with a parent, and keyed calls, read doc, log_d, log_l, meta and nodes; a keyed replay reads the same and writes nothing; the two refusals (422 container value, 409 halted) run no statement warm. Asserted by tests/test_state_p02_contact_facets.py.

The whole report runs under DOC_LOCK in one write cycle: it serialises with every other document writer in the org, although it touches only the caller's node row and, for done/blocked, the parent's mailbox, mail_log, events and lifecycle.
The mail queue, events and lifecycle are org-wide document sections, so two reports to different parents still write the same rows in the legacy store.

The desktop engine wraps the app in engine/launch.py's TokenGate (outside the pinned backend module set, so no source span): every HTTP request needs X-Orgtree-Desktop-Token. A missing token is 401 'missing authentication; …', a wrong one 401 'invalid desktop token'. An agent credential is honoured only on POST /api/agent and the steer routes, so a VALID agent token on these GETs is refused 401 'agent credential is invalid or expired; …' — a misleading message, recorded as legacy behaviour. Pinned.

The operator token reaches every organization: there is no per-org operator scope. An unknown org is 404 (cached_org raises); a detail request for a node not in that org's tree is 404 'no such node: …'. Pinned.

Public kiosk access goes through PublicGateway, which resolves /k/<token>/… to exactly one kiosk-enabled org, 404s any other org or unknown token, applies the _public_denied matrix and marks the request public; the view then scrubs host paths, session ids and external handles (org-view.wire). Pinned with the gateway wrapped around the app directly. Only api.py's own main() starts that listener (ORGTREE_PUBLIC_PORT, policy allowing); the desktop launcher serves only the token-gated app.

The tree ETag hashes the org's save seq, supervisor.tree_state_fingerprint, the limits board's fetch stamp, the primed-restart record, the per-slug patch invalidation rev and a 30-second bucket. A matching If-None-Match answers 304 with no body before any load or build. The built body is cached per (slug, public) and one build at a time runs per key.

Recorded legacy behaviour: the first build of an org whose supervisor state is cold allocates per-node state entries while annotating, which changes the fingerprint, so the ETag that first response carried is already stale. Revalidating with it returns 200 and a new tag; revalidating with the new tag returns 304. Pinned.

Archived nodes are summarised in the tree (detail false, charter_line, lineage_count, read_only, detail_rev, only the last turn) and the payload carries archived_defaults once. The detail route finds the named node in the tree, empties its children, annotates it in full and, for an archived seat only, recomputes detail_rev. Pinned.

Recorded legacy defect, desktop-managed mode with warming enabled: annotating a live node asks warmpool.process_control_status for its control state, whose eligibility check runs the deployment gate and catches only RuntimeError. desktop_policy.validate raises ValueError for an org document carrying kiosk (or sandbox, or disk_mb), so such an org's admin tree and node detail answer 500 'ValueError: Not available in desktop MVP: kiosk'. The public view returns before that check and answers 200. Pinned.

Source read set: the shared cached_org snapshot (eager document; mail, asks and org_inbox materialise on first touch), Org.tree() over every node, the supervisor's per-node runtime state, the account registry rows and ambient provider paths, the limits and usage caches, kiosk config, sandbox disk usage and hub network status. Cold, every build reads doc, log_d, log_l, meta and nodes of the org's own store. Recorded cross-org read (legacy, not endorsed; P02 finding): every ADMIN tree build, cold and warm, also reads the doc table of the other orgs on the data root through store.local_net_slugs, declared as foreign statements; warm, those are the build's only statements. The public gateway resolves /k/<token> through api._kiosk_token_map, which is rebuilt on a 5-second cache by reading every org's store in the ASGI wrapper, before any census attempt exists (P02 kiosk_token_scan: every statement unbound, no census record). The public rows ran with that map pinned fresh, so a real public request made after the cache expires carries this every-org read as well (see org-view.instrumentation).

Refusals: no token (401) and a bad kiosk token (404, answered by the gateway) run no statement and leave no census record; an unknown node (404) and the desktop-mode kiosk 500 (the recorded org-view.wire defect) run no statement warm. Neither route saves. Measured on already-migrated synthetic data: no document section changes for the tree, the detail route or the public tree. The tree cache, the per-slug invalidation rev and the supervisor state entries annotate allocates are process memory.

facts: TokenGate closes a websocket without the desktop token with code 4401 before the route runs (pinned). A kiosk socket arrives through PublicGateway and joins flagged public. The route itself checks no org: a token-holding socket for an organization that does not exist is accepted and joins an empty room (pinned).

Client text is received and ignored (it only keeps the socket alive). A disconnect leaves the room; a failed send drops the socket from the room. Public sockets receive the public projection of any typed segments in a frame, admin sockets the full one. Pinned for join, ignore and leave.
The route reads no store or document state: it accepts, registers the socket and loops on receive. Frame content is produced elsewhere (save-driven 'changed', node events, UI mail sparks, streams).
No document write: room and public-set membership are process memory. Pinned: joining and leaving change no document section.
Ordering rests on a per-slug, per-process rev counter; 'changed' is coalesced over 0.4 s; there is no durable cursor, so a client that misses frames catches up with one full tree fetch (sync_rev).

The agent door authenticates the caller (401/403) and refuses halt and killswitch (409) before the write cycle, as for every agent tool. Pinned for a halted sender.

Addressing (§7.2, Org.post_mail) for an in-org agent recipient: the sender may reach any descendant, its parent (one hop up), a sibling (same parent), or anyone whose audience it holds. Everything else is refused 422 '<sender> may not address <to> — …'. Pinned: a cousin and a grandparent are refused; a reply from a deep report succeeds once the sender holds the audience its superior's mail granted. A node may address itself: the sibling clause is trivially true for sender == target (recorded, D-165).

§7.3: mail or a notice from an ancestor to a NON-child descendant that does not already hold the reverse audience grants the recipient an audience to reply to the sender directly (an 'audiences' row and the warning 'audience granted: <to> may now reply to <sender> directly'). Pinned for both tools; a second send grants nothing.
The user: only a top-level agent, or a holder of a user audience, may message 'user'; others are refused 422. orgtree_send_notice refuses the user and every outside address.

Outside parties (@org: and @net:, orgtree_message only): only agents; never from a sealed kiosk (read from source, not exercised); the sender must hold the ORG-INBOX (EXTERN) audience (the held-handle bypass left with the second stage of the external-chat retirement, docket the-external-chat-mcp-server-cannot-reach-the-v2, which also refuses every new response-handle grant). A top-level sender without it is auto-granted it by the send (with multi-holder off, every previous holder is revoked — read from source, not exercised); anyone else is refused 422. Addressing the org's own slug or own network identity is refused. The @ext: and @mcp: forms are retired and refuse 422, a new @mcp: send answering ledger.MCP_RETIRED before any audience or kiosk check (the external-chat server was retired by user ruling, docket the-external-chat-mcp-server-cannot-reach-the-v2; historical @mcp: rows stay readable). Pinned for @org: (top auto-grant, deep refused, self refused), @mcp: and @ext:.

Arguments pass _norm_args (a container 'to' or 'body' refuses 422 '<field> must be text, not <type>'). The recipient is resolved ONCE before anything records: 'user' is the user unless an agent is named user; a bare name that is no node here resolves to the one matching local org (@org:), else a hub peer (@net:); an old @mcp: correspondent no longer captures a bare name, and an ambiguous name refuses. An unmatched name refuses 422 'NOT DELIVERED — there is no agent named …' and queues nothing. Pinned for an unknown name and for a bare local-org name.

orgtree_message: kind defaults to 'message' and any other text is accepted verbatim, except 'notice', which refuses (only orgtree_send_notice mints it). urgent is only for the user and needs a nonblank urgent_reason; a reason without urgent refuses. Attachments go only to the user or @net: (at most 10; @net: files must lie inside the sender's scratch space and be at most 25 MB); for an agent they refuse. Pinned.
Recorded legacy behaviour: an empty, whitespace-only or missing body is accepted, stored and delivered (and drives the recipient). A self-send is accepted and drives the sender itself.

A recipient that is archived receives the mail deferred (stored, recipient_state archived, no drive) with a warning that nothing reads it until a rehire; an unrecoverable recipient refuses. @net: refuses without an enabled hub or when the name is not on a connected hub's roster.
TX_POST, in the resident write cycle ending in save_org. Measured with the committed document read cold, by recipient class:

an agent (live or archived): one mail row in the recipient's box (from, kind, body, relationship, message_id, operation_id, recv_seq), one mail_log row, one 'mail' event, one accepted lifecycle row (delivery mailbox) and the recipient's mail_seq/mailbox_id; plus one audiences row when §7.3 grants one.
the user: one user_inbox row (with urgent and urgent_reason when urgent), one 'mail' event and one accepted lifecycle row (delivery user_inbox).
an outside party: one org_inbox row {id, dir out, peer, body, at, by}, one 'mail' event, plus the EXTERN audience row when auto-granted, plus for @net: the hub spool entry, in the same save.
A keyed call adds op_receipts and op_receipts_meta in the same save. A keyed replay and every refusal commit nothing. Pinned for each class.

Coverage class TX_POST for both tools. A keyed orgtree_op_call admits the key inside the write cycle and files an applied receipt immediately before save, so the mail and its receipt commit together. The retained result keeps only delivered, deferred and id. A keyed replay returns the replay envelope without posting again, pinging, sparking or broadcasting. Pinned for both tools.

Observed at the callback boundary with spies: an in-org message sparks mail_notify(org, sender, recipient) inside the write cycle and, after the save, pings the recipient once through supervisor.send_message (wake default, mail_ping, ping_reason 'agent_mail'); a notice sparks the same and then steers once with wake=False and ping_reason 'notice'; a deferred (archived) recipient is sparked but never pinged. Mail to the user sparks '@user' and pings nobody. Every accepted send ends with hub_changed.

Outside parties: @org: sparks 'org_inbox' and, after the save, calls supervisor.interorg_send(this org, destination org, body), which writes into the DESTINATION org's own inbox; a new @mcp: send is refused before anything is filed; @net: stages the spool entry in the same save and then calls net.kick to wake the sender daemon.

orgtree_request_credits and orgtree_reallocate come through the agent door (401/403, halt and killswitch 409, as for every agent tool); the decision route is an operator route behind the desktop TokenGate (engine/launch.py, outside the pinned set), so an agent credential is refused 401 there (pinned).

credits.request: only a top-level agent, or a holder of a user audience, may ask the user for credits; others are refused 422 'only top-level agents (or holders of a user audience) may ask the user for credits directly …'. A headless org refuses every request. Pinned for a deep agent.

credits.reallocate: the caller needs downward authority over the target (Org._require_authority: a strict ancestor), so reallocating oneself or one's superior is refused 422 '<actor> has no authority over <node> — authority is downward only (§7.1)'; the target must be live. A positive delta is drawn up the parent chain (_chain_acquire, cascading when cascade_alloc is on); a top-level target is bounded by the top-level grant cap. Pinned.
credits.decide: the operator decides as the user; any pending request of the org can be approved, counter-offered (any legal amount, including a reduction down to the committed floor) or denied.

credits.request: new_limit is the requested TOTAL, parsed as a number and rounded up to a whole credit ('new_limit must be a number …' otherwise); a limit at or below the current grant withdraws a pending request (or reports nothing to request) without error; a reason is required; zero headroom refuses outright; a second request AMENDS the pending one (rev + 1) rather than adding another. Request ids are 'cr' plus the count of stored requests plus one. Pinned.

credits.reallocate: delta is parsed with _arg_num ('delta must be a number (got …)' otherwise); the resulting grant is rounded UP to a whole credit, so a fractional delta can move a whole credit (+0.3 on 7 gives 8); a negative delta cannot exceed the target's unused credits ('<node> has only N unused; the rest is committed'); a zero delta is accepted as a no-op. Pinned.

credits.decide: only a pending request is decidable ('no pending credit request …' otherwise, including a second decision); action must be approve or deny; approving a request whose agent is no longer live marks it moot and changes no grant; dry=true previews a granted amount without writing and needs granted. Pinned.

Measured with the committed document read cold. credits.request: credit_requests and one event (a new or amended request, or a withdrawal); a no-op answer writes nothing. credits.reallocate: the target's grant (nodes), grant_changed notices to the target and its parent (notices, notice_log), and a 'reallocate' event; a zero delta writes only the event. credits.decide: the request row (status, granted, notice, answer_mail) and events, plus for approve/counter the grant change and its notices, plus the decision mail to the agent (mail, mail_log, lifecycle, the agent's mail_seq, and a user_outbox copy); a moot approve writes only the request row and an event. Refusals write nothing. A keyed agent call adds op_receipts and op_receipts_meta in the same save. Pinned.

orgtree_request_credits is TX_POST and orgtree_reallocate TX: a keyed call files an applied receipt in the same save and a replay returns the replay envelope with no second change. The retained result keys do not match the results: request_credits retains (id, routed, deferred), which its result never carries, so its receipt keeps NOTHING of the request (recorded legacy defect); reallocate retains (node, delta, grant) and keeps only grant. The decision route has no operation receipt. Pinned.

The two agent tools ping nobody and spark nothing; like every accepted agent call they end with hub_changed. A decision that produces a notice posts it as user mail to a live agent, then sparks mail_notify(org, @user, agent) and pings the agent once (supervisor.send_message, mail_ping, ping_reason 'credit_decision'); a moot decision sends nothing. The decision route always ends with hub_changed. Pinned with spies.

Source read set: the caller and target nodes, the parent chain up to the root for a positive delta (_chain_acquire, free amounts and child grants), tier prices, the org's credit caps and headless flag, and the credit_requests list; the decision route loads the org under DOC_LOCK through load_org, which inside the lock is served the per-org resident document (store._load_org's resident fast path; a fresh parse only on a miss or a dirty repeat hand-out), not the cached_org snapshot the agent door reads.

Observed by the P02 per-operation probe (tools/p02_operation_contacts.py; docs/state-system/p02-operation-contacts.md) (synthetic data, v3 56a9c22) for every outcome the clause names, cold and warm, answering both questions above: request new, :amend and :withdraw; reallocate up, :down and :deep; decide approve, :counter, :deny, :moot and :dry; plus nothing-to-request, a zero and a fractional delta, keyed fresh and replay for both agent tools, the refusals and a locality control. Cold, every outcome reads doc, log_d, log_l, meta and nodes of the org's own store. Warm, a request or a reallocation reads doc, log_l, meta and nodes; a decision reads at least meta and nodes, up to all five, as the resident document needs; a warm dry run runs no statement. No row makes an unknown contact or touches another org's store.

Writes, all inside a transaction: a request, amendment or withdrawal writes doc and log_l; a reallocation doc, log_l and nodes, and a zero delta only its log_l event; an approved, countered or denied decision doc, log_d, log_l and nodes; a moot decision doc and log_l. Nothing-to-request, a keyed replay, a dry run and every refusal write nothing. Warm, the argument refusals (a non-number, not top level, upward, self, a bad action, a dry run without granted, an id not pending) run no statement; a request without a reason reads only meta; the committed-floor refusal reads what a reallocation reads. The agent credential on the decision route is refused 401 before any census attempt. Asserted by tests/test_state_p02_contact_facets.py.

Each operation runs in one document write cycle under DOC_LOCK (the decision route takes DOC_LOCK itself around load_org and save_org); grants, the parent chain's free amounts and credit_requests are org-document state, so every funding change serialises with every other writer.

Native design r7 (docket design-the-native-conflict-predicate-and-isolati artifact r7, sha256 24e86a19f95b47ef2a2acabfbc8d8f4861268f555692167ea019c9c80f160792; approved by review artifact r10, sha256 8be9323173dd1ae785f66328a8481a12bf86c7f2c816797c1c9c496c01ea895b): the design half is answered in part: C2a pair P2 (the payer's capacity row holds committed child obligations in unpriced terms, the sum of child grants and child seat counts per tier; every obligation writer updates it; island writers take it FOR UPDATE before computing free and outside writers take it FOR UPDATE first; the catalog version row is share-locked and prices apply at read), section 6.4's reallocate row and its funding requirement, and C2a pair P7 for a credit-request filing (the asker's authority-epoch row is bumped, so a retire or dissolve either moots it or makes it refuse). Credit-request approval appears only as a C2a P2 outside writer (it updates the payer's capacity row). Not covered by r7: approval's own conflict set (legacy checks that the request is still pending and computes the delta from the current grant under DOC_LOCK, ledger.py credit_request_action; native has to order a conditional pending-state transition before the delta is computed from the grant read after the funding locks, or two concurrent decisions both apply it); the filing's one-pending-request-per-node rule (P7 does not require the authority-epoch bump before the pending lookup, so two concurrent filings could both create a pending request); and r7 section 8 has no schedule for deep bubbling or a concurrent decision. Qualification of the covered part is scheduled at P03: Q-C8 and Q-C12 (b).

Native design extension r3 (docket extend-the-native-conflict-and-predicate-design artifact r8, sha256 f5ee496781b4c2464a3ee723e9a740f5330bb61f516f9279e2e38a3c655af99c; approved by review artifact r11, sha256 4f94e78ccec0ba8a942e277e0c73f5d298f184c0dfb61d2e25cb73ce50c30b8d): the design half is answered for what r7 left open: section 4.13. A decision is one READ COMMITTED command that anchors the agent (FOR SHARE), then compare-and-sets the request row from pending BEFORE any amount is computed, so a second decision on one request refuses and an approve racing a deny, or two counter-offers, cannot both apply; it then takes r7's reallocate funding locks with the user as actor, reads the grant after them and computes the delta; an approve of an agent that is no longer live moots the request by its own compare-and-set from pending, before the decision's (a deny does not look at liveness). The filing's one-pending rule is a partial unique index on (organization, node) WHERE status is pending. In a kiosk organization every writer of a top-level holding meets on E8's kiosk pool row (E-D17 (b) amends r7's reallocate row). Decisions E-D14 and E-D15. With r7's P2, reallocate row and P7 (above) this covers the clause's design half, except in a kiosk organization: there E-D15 deliberately keeps an organization-wide kiosk pool row (E8) that every top-level holding writer locks exclusively, which the clause's 'no org-wide credit counter' excludes. That exception is a coordinator-accepted departure from v6, scoped to kiosk organizations (E-D15; coordinator ruling, decision 2 of item p01-cite-the-approved-native-design-extension-r3), not the clause as worded; its schedule is Q-FD5. The qualified half is scheduled at P03 (E-D18): Q-FD1 (two decisions on one request), Q-FD2 (a decision racing an amendment, and two concurrent filings), Q-FD3 (a decision racing a retire or mark_unrecoverable), Q-FD4 (deep bubbling), Q-FD5 (the kiosk pool) and r7's Q-C8 and Q-C12 (b).
