facts: The agent door labels and classifies the two tools; the decision route is labelled by the access middleware. P02's per-operation record covers all three (below).

Observed by the P02 per-operation probe (tools/p02_operation_contacts.py; docs/state-system/p02-operation-contacts.md) (synthetic data, v3 56a9c22): a loss-accounted per-operation record for every funding row, cold and warm (one census record matching the harness, every write inside a transaction), except the decision route's agent-credential refusal, which is answered before any census attempt. Agent-level locality, answering the question above: a request changes no agent's mail, notices or row; a reallocation changes only the target's row and notices, and for a grandchild its parent's notices too; an approved, countered or denied decision changes only the requester's mail, mail_log and row, plus its notice when the grant changes (approve, counter); moot and dry change no agent. The control control:funding-third-agent (a reallocation that also posts mail to a sibling) is flagged, and no other funding row writes a third agent's mail or row.

One physical read falls outside that set without belonging to the operation. A warm raise or zero delta that directly follows a row which changed f-kid reads f-kid's node row (P02 records it as a third-agent read, and its third_sites names orgtree.api:_agent_identity as the first product frame). The statement is the agent door's snapshot refresh: api._agent_identity calls store.cached_org, whose _assemble_snapshot re-reads every node id the org's writers recorded in _changed_nodes since the last snapshot (the `for nid in nids` loop). A reordered run (P01 S2f artifact r1, fkid-order-33c6cf2.json) shows it appears only after a row that changed f-kid, with those frames. So under concurrent activity a warm operation's physical read set also covers node rows any earlier write in the org changed, bounded by those changes and not by the operation's own agents; logical locality is unaffected. Native negative controls are the P03 gate, not a clause of this legacy facet (S2d decision 1, reviewer ruling on 803227e). Asserted by tests/test_state_p02_contact_facets.py.

orgtree_hire and orgtree_staff come through the agent door (401/403, halt and killswitch 409, as for every agent tool). The provider gate (provider_hire_gate: the tier's provider must be enabled, installed and signed in; kiosks hold out Codex, Antigravity and OpenRouter) runs first for a hire and is a machine-state check outside the pinned set: the boundary tests patch it off and say so.

Hire destination: `target` (or its older spelling `parent`), defaulting to the caller, must be the caller or a live descendant (check_placement: '"<t>" is outside your subtree …'); only the user hires at the top level; hire_type='superior' inserts the seat above a seat in the caller's subtree (above a top-level seat only the user may). Pinned.

The new seat's scope is clamped strictly to its parent's for an agent caller: folders, every tool switch and visibility cannot exceed the parent's, and permission_mode/effort/team_charter go through set_scope, which caps permission_mode at the caller's own. Audiences use orgtree_audience's vocabulary and rules ('user' only for a top-level caller, the caller's own id, a live peer, or the caller's direct superior); a target the caller could not grant refuses the whole call. Pinned for 'user' from a non-top-level caller and for the caller's own id.

orgtree_staff inherits the seat authority unchanged (_hire_seat or _rehire_seat) and the docket authority of work_create/work_update; in rehire mode the caller needs authority over the archived node (Org.rehire: a strict ancestor, or the node's own bearer successor). An account named with `account` is validated by registry.validate_selection.

Hire: an ordinary (subordinate) hire has no defaults — add_dirs, tools (every switch) and org_visibility are required at the door and a charter by the ledger; hire_type='superior' refuses those three and permission_mode instead (it takes the anchor's). The tier must be known ('unknown tier …' lists the known ones); grant must be a non-negative whole number; seat + grant must be free on the chain from the destination up to the caller (_chain_acquire, bubbling when cascade_hire is on), else 'not enough free credits on the chain …'; max depth and max children refuse; audiences entries must be text; kickoff_kind 'notice' is refused. Every refusal is checked before the first mutation or discarded with the unsaved document. Pinned.

Staff: action is create or update ('orgtree_staff writes the docket with action …' otherwise); update needs slug; an OMITTED action is inferred (update when slug is given, else create) — the selector DSL cannot express that inference, so the registry's selector cases name the action; staff_mode is hire or rehire and must agree with `node` (a node means rehire); the docket half's own validation applies (a create needs a title). Staffing in rehire mode a node that is already LIVE is not refused: Org.rehire answers 'already live — nothing to do' and the item is still created and assigned (recorded legacy behaviour). Pinned.

Measured with the committed document read cold. A hire writes the new node (nodes) and a hire event; lifecycle.hired notices go to the parent and the new seat's peers other than the caller (notices, notice_log); a kickoff adds the kickoff mail (mail, mail_log, lifecycle); audiences write audiences and the grant's own mail; work_item writes work_items and the assignment mail. A superior insertion re-parents the anchor under the new seat, which reports to the anchor's old parent; the inserted seat's own cost is paid out of the anchor's grant (anchor 6 -> 5, inserted seat 6), budget-neutral above. Pinned.

Staff writes the seat as above, then the item in the SAME save (work_items plus the assignment mail to the seat); an update that moves an item also tells its previous owner with an @system notice; a staffing with no stored summary gets one generated boundary line (result staffing_boundary). A refusal anywhere writes nothing, EXCEPT staff in rehire mode with a `name`: the rename runs before the transaction (supervisor.rename_node takes the lock itself and moves folders), so a later refusal leaves the node renamed and still archived, and the refusal says so. A keyed call adds op_receipts and op_receipts_meta in the same save. Pinned.

orgtree_hire and orgtree_staff are TX_POST; staff in rehire mode is PRE when it carries a name (the rename moves folders before any transaction) and TX_POST without one (opreceipts.coverage). A keyed call files an applied receipt in the same save; a replay returns the replay envelope and changes nothing. Retained result keys: hire keeps node, started and account (its allowlisted name, tier and grant are not in the result); staff keeps node, started, item, created or updated, assigned_to and account. The account_binding slice (result_slice, shared with rehire and retool) is not specified here. Pinned.

A started seat is driven exactly ONCE after the save (supervisor.send_message, mail_ping, no ping_reason), whatever started it: a kickoff, a work_item or staff assignment, a rehire with waiting mail, or an audience grant that wakes the grantee. Without one of those nothing is driven and the result says the seat is IDLE. Each kickoff and each assignment sparks mail_notify(org, caller, seat), so staff with a kickoff sparks twice and posts two request mails. Every accepted call ends with one hub_changed. Recorded legacy behaviour: a hire started only by an audience grant is told 'its first turn starts on your kickoff' although no kickoff was sent. Pinned with spies.

Source read set: the caller, the destination and its chain up to the caller (free amounts, grants, scopes, depth and child counts), tier prices and the tier ceiling, the org's defaults (visibility, tools, account, cascade_hire), the audience table, and for staff the work items; the harness choice for an OpenRouter tier is a provider read made before DOC_LOCK (new_hire_harness).

Observed by the P02 per-operation probe (tools/p02_operation_contacts.py; docs/state-system/p02-operation-contacts.md) (synthetic data, v3 56a9c22) for every class the clause names, cold and warm, answering both questions above: hire plain, :kickoff, :target, :superior, :audiences and :work-item; staff create, update (an item passes from its owner to a new seat) and create in rehire mode; plus keyed fresh and replay for both tools, the refusals and a locality control. Cold, every class reads doc, log_d, log_l, meta and nodes of the org's own store; warm, every class reads at least doc, log_l, meta and nodes. No row makes an unknown contact or touches another org's store. Not exercised: the OpenRouter harness choice (new_hire_harness, a provider read), because the fixture hires haiku and the provider gate is stubbed; the clause does not name it.

Every successful call writes log_l and nodes of the org's store, and a call that starts the seat (kickoff, audiences, work item, and every staff call) writes all five tables. Every hire and staff call, refused and replayed ones too, also journals in the tool_waits sidecar (both are managed-wait tools, toolwait.invoke): it writes operations and dead_letters and runs eight DDL statements outside a transaction, each row's only writes outside a transaction (recorded, not endorsed). The refusals (422) write nothing to the org's store: outside the subtree reads all five tables first; not enough credits, an unknown tier, a bad staff action and a missing title run no statement on it. A keyed replay writes nothing to it. Asserted by tests/test_state_p02_contact_facets.py.

Each call runs in one document write cycle under DOC_LOCK, except the rehire-mode rename (its own lock, before) and the provider/harness reads (before the lock); the seat, the chain's credits and the item are org-document state, so staffing serialises with every other writer.

facts: The agent door labels and classifies both tools; the seat's first turn is a supervisor drive after the save. P02's per-operation record covers both (below).

Observed by the P02 per-operation probe (tools/p02_operation_contacts.py; docs/state-system/p02-operation-contacts.md) (synthetic data, v3 56a9c22): a loss-accounted per-operation record for every staffing row, cold and warm, refusals and replays included (one census record matching the harness per row). Agent-level locality, answering the question above against a WIDENED set: the caller, the destination chain, the new or rehired seat and a moved item's previous owner, plus the new seat's parent and that parent's other live children (lifecycle.hired, relations report and peer) and, for a superior insertion, the anchor and the anchor's reports (lifecycle.inserted, which tells the new parent (parent), its other children (peer), the anchor (target), the anchor's reports (child) and the seat itself (self)). The widening follows the user ruling recorded at ledger.hire's notices ("every affected agent is told, WHOEVER acted"; relayed by the coordinator as the 2026-09-07 ruling) and the coordinator's ruling of 2026-09-24 that this fan-out is intended, not a defect; it grows with the number of peers. Mail goes only to the new seat (its first-turn request) and, for a staff update, to the item's previous owner. The control control:staffing-third-agent (a kickoff hire whose first-turn drive also mails a sibling) is flagged, and no other staffing row writes a third agent's mail or row.

Four warm rows also physically read one node row outside that set, and P02's third_sites names orgtree.api:_agent_identity for each. Each is the node the previous probe row changed, re-read by the agent door's snapshot refresh: the carry-over settled in S2f (see funding.instrumentation), not a contact of the call. Native negative controls are the P03 gate, not a clause of this legacy facet (S2d decision 1, reviewer ruling on 803227e). Asserted by tests/test_state_p02_contact_facets.py.

POST /api/orgs/{slug}/ops is an operator route behind the desktop TokenGate (engine/launch.py, outside the pinned set): an agent credential is refused 401 (pinned). The operator acts as `actor`, which defaults to the user; naming an agent as `actor` makes the ledger apply THAT agent's authority and rules — an agent-actor hire needs the no-defaults fields and an agent-actor reallocation is downward-only (pinned). Kiosk visitors reach the same handler through the public gateway (/k/<token>/api/orgs/{slug}/ops, which does not deny it): a visitor hire and reallocation run with the visitor's `actor` as sent (default the user), raise_ceiling is not honoured and the ceiling bridge is stripped, the kiosk ceiling clamps the new seat, and a visitor preview is refused 403 (pinned).

operator.hire: the user hires at the top level (no `parent`) or under any live parent; `above` inserts the new seat above an existing report of `parent` ('insert-superior: does not report to

' otherwise), with check_placement's rules. The provider gate runs first (machine state, patched off by the boundary tests). operator.reallocate: the user may move any node's grant, drawn up the parent chain as for credits.reallocate; a top-level target is bounded by the top-level grant cap.

The F1b variants (operator.rename through operator.revoke-dir, and operator.preview) share the route's door and actor rule: an agent credential is refused 401, and naming an agent as `actor` applies that agent's authority (an agent-actor rename or retire outside its subtree is refused 'X has no authority over Y'; an agent-actor retire of itself with live reports is refused). rescind and delete are user-only in the ledger ('only the user may rescind …', 'only the user may delete agents …'), and a promotion to the top level is user-only ('only the user promotes agents to top level …'). A preview's actor, when not the user, must be a live node. Pinned by tests/test_state_operator_variants_boundary.py against docs/state-system/operator-variants-boundary.json.

operator.hire: tier and name are required ('hire needs tier and name'); `preview` is refused for hire ("preview does not support operator operation 'hire'", 422, nothing written — the selector admits it and the refusal is part of this contract). A user hire takes defaults for omitted scope (the org's at the top level, the parent's below) and clamps explicit scope to the parent leniently, with warnings; with `above`, any add_dirs, tools, org_visibility or permission_mode sent are replaced by the anchor's and a warning names them (result scope_from_anchor). effort, prefer_reserve and account_fallback are applied with the hire in the same save; the ledger's own hire predicates (known tier, whole grant, credits on the chain, depth and child caps) apply. A repeated hire with the same name seats a second agent under a suffixed id. Pinned.

operator.reallocate: delta is required ('reallocate needs delta') and is a float on the wire; the resulting grant is rounded up to a whole credit (+0.5 moves a whole credit); Org.reallocate's rules apply as for credits.reallocate ('<node> has only N unused; the rest is committed'). `preview: true` is a DIFFERENT, read-only operation (statepreview.preview answers {operation, applied: false, …} and writes nothing): the selector excludes it with all[equals(op, reallocate), not(truthy_text(preview))]. Pinned.

F1b variants: 'rename needs node and name', 'switch_model needs tier', 'demote needs new_parent', 'revoke_dir needs dir', 'unknown op …', and cheap_compact of a node that is not live ('… replaces a LIVE agent's session'); a preview of hire, rename, cheap_compact or rehire is refused ('preview does not support operator operation …'). From source: cheap_compact with if_idle refuses a busy node 409, and a reseed of an archived node is refused ('… rehire it instead'). Pinned by tests/test_state_operator_variants_boundary.py against docs/state-system/operator-variants-boundary.json, except the two source clauses.

Measured with the committed document read cold. operator.hire writes the new node, a hire event and lifecycle.hired notices (nodes, events, notices, notice_log — the acting user is never the parent, so the parent is always told); `above` re-parents the anchor under the new seat in the same save. operator.reallocate writes the target's grant (and inflated grants up the chain) with its event and grant_changed notices (nodes, events, notices, notice_log). One load/mutate/save under DOC_LOCK; a refusal writes nothing. Pinned.

F1b variants, measured with the committed document read cold: rename writes nodes, events and the renamed seat's notices; retire writes nodes, events and lifecycle.retired to the parent; rescind writes the retire plus a rescind event, claws the stake back from the parent's grant and tells the parent (lifecycle.rescinded); cheap_compact writes the bearer row, the fresh session and notices to the seat and its parent; rehire writes nodes, events and lifecycle.rehired to the seat and its parent; dissolve writes lifecycle.dissolved to the parent and peers; delete removes the subtree's records, rewrites the swept lists (asks, scope_requests, watchdogs) and tells the parent (lifecycle.deleted); switch_model writes lifecycle.model_switched to the node and its parent; promote, demote and move write lifecycle.moved to the old and new parent or peers and the node; reseed of an unrecoverable node writes a lost-generation bearer row nid@gen and lifecycle.reseeded to the seat and its parent; revoke_dir writes nodes and events only. promote, demote and move also rewrite node rows along ledger._move's credit path: the moved seat's parent, and the grant of every seat the stake passes, released hop by hop from the old parent up to the lowest common ancestor and acquired from below it down to the new parent (the ancestor itself is not written). A promotion to the top level has @user as that ancestor, so it rewrites the whole old chain up to the top-level seat, and an ancestor above the old parent is told nothing unless it is also a new peer (P02 finding on this family; measured by P01 on top > mid > leaf > deep: promoting deep rewrites leaf, mid and top and tells deep, leaf, top and top2, not mid); a demote or a move within a subtree stops below the common ancestor. reseed of a live node and every preview write nothing; every refusal writes nothing. Pinned by tests/test_state_operator_variants_boundary.py against docs/state-system/operator-variants-boundary.json.
The operator ops door files no operation receipt and takes no op key: a lost response cannot be replayed, and a retried hire creates another seat (pinned: the second seat gets a suffixed id).

The F1b variants, like hire and reallocate, file no operation receipt and take no operation key. Pinned by tests/test_state_operator_variants_boundary.py against docs/state-system/operator-variants-boundary.json.

Both operations end with one hub_changed and drive nobody: an operator hire has no kickoff (org_op drives only a rehire's waiting mail), and nothing sparks mail_notify. The preview variant broadcasts nothing. Pinned with spies.

F1b variants: operator rename reaps (supervisor.remote_reap), broadcasts hub_changed and notifies 'renamed' — unlike the agent door's rename, which does neither of the first two; retire, dissolve and rescind interrupt the target before the lock (interrupt_before_archive), and the agent door's recorded defect holds here too: an agent-actor rescind and an agent-actor self-retire with live reports are refused after the interrupt; retire, dissolve, delete, rescind and cheap_compact reap after the save; delete takes NO pre-archive interrupt and calls supervisor.forget(slug, deleted), which drops the deleted seats' runtime state and removes their scratch directories (source); cheap_compact copies the transcript; a rehire whose seat has waiting mail drives it once with 'Mail above arrived while you were archived …' (mail_ping, ping_reason 'rehire_waited'), a different wording and reason from the agent door's. Every accepted operation ends with one hub_changed, reseed's no-op included; a preview broadcasts nothing. Pinned by tests/test_state_operator_variants_boundary.py against docs/state-system/operator-variants-boundary.json, except forget's file removal.

Source read set: the org loaded under DOC_LOCK through load_org, which inside the lock is served the per-org resident document (store._load_org's resident fast path; a fresh parse only on a miss or a dirty repeat hand-out), the parent chain's free amounts and grants, tier prices and ceilings, the org's scope defaults and the anchor's scope for `above`; the harness choice for an OpenRouter tier is a provider read made before DOC_LOCK (new_hire_harness).

Observed by the P02 per-operation probe (tools/p02_operation_contacts.py; docs/state-system/p02-operation-contacts.md) (synthetic data, v3 ebad321) for every class the clause names, cold and warm, answering both questions above, as the operator (@user) on the desktop token: hire at the top level, under a parent (:under) and above an anchor (:above); reallocate up, :down and :top-level; plus a fractional delta, the refusals and a locality control. Cold, every class reads doc, log_d, log_l, meta and nodes of the org's own store; warm, only meta and nodes. No row makes an unknown contact or touches another org's store. Not exercised: the OpenRouter harness choice (new_hire_harness, a provider read), because the fixture hires haiku and the provider gate is stubbed, and the kiosk visitor path to this door; the clause names neither.

The refusals write nothing to the org's store: a hire with no name, an unknown tier, an above-hire whose anchor does not report to the named parent, a reallocation with no delta, one below the committed floor, and a named agent actor with no authority over its superior (422); the agent credential is refused 401 before any census attempt. Asserted by tests/test_state_p02_contact_facets.py.

F1b variants, from source: each operation loads the org under DOC_LOCK in _org_op_locked; retire, dissolve and rescind load it once more before the lock for their authority pre-guard, and rename loads it in supervisor.rename_node. switch_model reads the provider gate, the account rule (check_switch_account) and the live busy state; cheap_compact with if_idle reads the live busy state; a preview loads the org under DOC_LOCK and simulates the operation on a detached copy (statepreview.preview), never saving. These reads are not observed by P02 (operator-ops.variant-instrumentation).
Each operation is one whole-document write cycle under DOC_LOCK (load_org, mutate, save_org), so it serialises with every other writer; the harness read happens before the lock.

All four routes are operator routes behind the desktop TokenGate (engine/launch.py, outside the pinned set): an agent credential is refused 401 (pinned for staffing-options and the quick-staff commit). The commit acts as the user throughout: request mode mails the assignee as @user, and the immediate modes call _staff_call(org, slug, USER, …), so the seat and the docket write carry the user's authority and the staffing.staff-update rules. Kiosk visitors are not examined here.

Provider discovery (api._providers_payload, the OpenRouter catalog, account boards), the provider gate, account reasons and advertised efforts are machine state read through the staffcache snapshot; the boundary tests patch them to a fixed offer and recompute the snapshot on every read.

Preview and commit: the ticket must be backlogged and not archived ('Quick staff is available only for backlogged tickets. Reopen the menu.'); the mode is the app setting quick_staff_behavior (request | under_assignee | top_level), falling back to top_level when the assignee is not live (context). The commit refuses a selection whose mode, configured_mode or owner no longer match ('The staffing behavior or assignee changed. …'), an effort or an account without a tier, an immediate mode without a tier ('Immediate staffing requires a model. …'), and in request mode an account unless the quick_staff_request_accounts setting is on ('Request staffing cannot pin an account …'); the tier is re-checked by quickstaff.check_choice over a snapshot read with max_age COMMIT_MAX_AGE (30 s) and allow_stale False. Pinned.

staffing-options answers the org's tiers in catalog order, omitting a tier the provider gate or tier ceiling blocks and an account-needing tier with no eligible account; discovery errors are reported in `errors`, never as an empty list. The quick-staff preview lists the offered models in request mode and, in the immediate modes, only tiers a trial hire (HireProbe) admits. Pinned for the fixed offer.

staffing-options, its refresh and the preview write nothing durable (pinned); the refresh changes only the in-process availability cache (staffcache: the snapshot is marked stale and the generation bumped).

Measured with the committed document read cold. Request mode: the ticket goes to open (working_on_next becomes ['Staff the ticket.'] when it was empty), the request mail to the assignee from @user (mail, mail_log, lifecycle, user_outbox, nodes), events, and the receipt quick_staff_receipts[request_id] on the item, in one save. Immediate modes: the seat and the item update exactly as _staff_call writes them, the previous owner's @system notice, under_assignee also a @user notice to the previous assignee, and the receipt, in one save; the seat is named from the ticket title. Refusals write nothing. Pinned.

The commit keeps its own idempotency receipt: quick_staff_receipts[request_id] = {selection, result} on the item, in the same save as the effect. The same request_id and selection returns the stored result with replayed: true and changes nothing; a request_id already used for a different selection is refused ('That staffing request id already belongs to a different selection.'). No op_receipts row is filed (the operator door has no op key). The other three routes have no receipt. Pinned.

After the commit's save: one hub_changed, then for each driven node (request mode: the assignee unless the mail was deferred; immediate modes: the new seat) mail_notify(org, @user, node) and one supervisor.send_message with mail_ping and ping_reason 'quick_staff' (the immediate modes also spark mail_notify once more from the staff assignment). A kickoff the send door does not accept undoes a request-mode commit (_quick_staff_undo, compare-and-set on the item rev) and 422s; in the immediate modes the seat stays and the result carries kickoff_failed. Recorded legacy defect: when the ticket had empty progress lists, the undo's work_update refuses 'both empty', escapes as an unhandled 500, and nothing is undone. staffing-options and the preview signal nothing; the refresh starts a background warm ('manual retry'). Pinned with spies.

Source read set: the staffcache snapshot (read OUTSIDE DOC_LOCK), then under DOC_LOCK the whole org loaded (load_org), the ticket and its owner's liveness, the org's tiers, ceilings and scope defaults, and for the immediate modes a trial hire per tier over the eager sections (HireProbe); the commit's harness choice is a provider read before the lock.

orgtree_op_lookup is a receipt VERB on POST /api/agent, not a tool card: it needs the caller's agent token (401 otherwise) and, like every agent tool, is refused 409 while the caller is halted or the org killswitch is latched (supervisor.halt.blocked runs first, pinned for a halted caller); it is then answered by _op_lookup_call BEFORE the restart/relaunch gates and the write cycle, because a lookup performs none of those operations. A caller can only ask about its OWN keys: the row is found by (caller node, key), so asking about another agent's key finds nothing and fences that key in the caller's own namespace (pinned).

op_key is required ('a lookup needs the `op_key` it is asking about') and for_tool is required ('a lookup needs `for_tool` …'); for_args is normalised exactly as admission normalises it, so the two fingerprints of one call agree. The row under the key is classified before any claim: a different fingerprint is `conflict`; a matching applied row is `applied` (also under a rotated epoch — durable positive evidence); a fence is reported as the fence; a call with the key executing in this process is `running`; a verb that never reaches the transaction is `unknown`/unsupported_operation; under a rotated epoch an absent row is `unknown`/epoch_rotated and nothing is fenced. Otherwise the key is FENCED and the answer is `not_applied` when the verb's coverage class makes absence provable, `unknown`/pre_transaction_step when the verb also works outside the transaction. Pinned.

The agent-side client (mcptool.call_api) asks only after the answer to a keyed call was LOST, under the original key and epoch, and never reissues the call itself. A lookup REFUSED as an unknown verb ("orgtree_op_lookup" in the refusal) means the backend predates receipts: the client answers state unknown, reason unsupported_build (fb501a21). Pinned with the transport patched.

Only a lookup that finds nothing (current epoch, receipted verb, not running) writes: one op_receipts row with outcome 'fenced' (op_receipts, op_receipts_meta) under DOC_LOCK in its own save, then witnessed. Every other answer writes nothing. The fence is what makes `not_applied` true: a delayed original under that key is refused at admission ('op_key refused (fenced) …', 422) and changes nothing. Pinned.

A lookup is never itself keyed (a question must not become an operation with its own key); its durable trace is the fence row. A repeated lookup of a fenced key answers from the fence (with its `at`) and writes nothing. Pinned.
A lookup drives nobody, sparks nothing and does not broadcast: it returns from agent_call before the dispatch tail that ends in hub_changed, including when it fences. Pinned with spies.

Source read set: under DOC_LOCK, the whole org loaded (load_org), the caller's node and generation, the custody epoch, the receipt row under (node, key) and its fingerprint subject; the in-process in-flight set; the verb's coverage class.

Observed by the P02 per-operation probe (tools/p02_operation_contacts.py; docs/state-system/p02-operation-contacts.md) (synthetic data, v3 f690e5e) for every answer the clause names, cold and warm, as the caller on the agent door: not_applied with a new fence, applied, conflict, and epoch-rotated (unknown, not fenced), plus a repeat lookup answered from the fence and, warm, a lookup of another agent's applied key. Cold, every answer reads doc, log_d, log_l, meta and nodes of the org's own store. Warm, the lookup is served the per-org resident under DOC_LOCK, so its store contact depends on the resident's state: the applied answer ran no statement, the repeat of a fence read only doc, log_l and meta, and the conflict and epoch-rotated answers, each following an answer that returned a receipt row, reloaded all five tables, because store._on_doc_lock_release drops a resident whose lazy log section a hold exposed (measured by v3-popout-review-opus55's mutant R1 on be8a05e, and repeated in P01 S2j: with that drop disabled, the warm conflict and epoch-rotated lookups run no statement). Only a new fence writes (doc and log_l, and meta cold); every other answer writes nothing. No row makes an unknown contact or touches another org's store. The refusals write nothing: halted (409), no op_key (422) and no for_tool (422); a bad token is refused 401 before any census attempt. Asserted by tests/test_state_p02_contact_facets.py.

The classify-then-fence is one DOC_LOCK transaction, so a delayed original either committed first (and is found applied) or is refused forever after; the `running` answer covers only this process's in-flight set.

The twelve tool contracts arrive on the agent door (POST /api/agent, api.agent_call) with an agent credential, and the caller is body.node; a halted caller or a latched org killswitch is refused 409 before any tool runs. The target is governed by the ledger's downward rule (Org._require_authority: the user, the system, or a strict ancestor of the target), refused as 'X has no authority over Y — authority is downward only'. Pinned by tests/test_state_lifecycle_boundary.py against docs/state-system/lifecycle-boundary.json for rename, retool, retire, dissolve, cheap_compact, swap and a real move. Recorded legacy defect (point 6 of lifecycle-tool-receipts-and-admission-keyed-rena): a move to the node's CURRENT parent returns its no-op (moved: false, changed: false, '<node> already reports to <parent> — nothing to do') from Org.move before promote or demote runs any authority check, and the agent door has no pre-guard, so ANY caller, an unrelated agent included, gets an accepted write cycle (a save, one hub_changed and, when keyed, a receipt) whose answer also confirms the node's parent. Pinned.

Acting on oneself differs per tool: retire allows the caller itself, but only as a leaf ('you have live reports …'); self_subjugate always acts on the caller; retool on oneself may set team_charter only ('you may not rewrite your OWN charter'); rename, dissolve and cheap_compact refuse the caller itself through the downward rule; swap checks both parties with allow_self, so an agent may swap itself with its own descendant; switch_model refuses the caller's own model ('you cannot switch your OWN model'). rehire also admits the caller's own knowledge bearer (successor == caller), which then joins as the caller's subordinate (source). Pinned, except the bearer case.

swap's own rules (Org.swap_seats): a swap of an agent with itself is refused ('a seat swap needs two different agents'); both parties must be live; when either party sits at the top level only the user may swap ('only the user reseats the top level …'), except through the internal voluntary-subjugation marker, which no API argument can set; a lineage bearer or a party with live lineage bearers is refused, and so is a swap that would land an agent on its own stack's branch or under an archived seat (source). Pinned by tests/test_state_lifecycle_boundary.py against docs/state-system/lifecycle-boundary.json, except the lineage and landing refusals.

The door's identity check (api._agent_identity) refuses 403 a caller whose seat is archived or replaced ('authenticated seat is archived or replaced …') and a credential minted for an earlier session generation ('agent credential is stale: session generation changed …'). So after a dissolve the archived seats can no longer call, and after a cheap compaction the seat's pre-compaction credential is refused. Pinned.

The two catalogue reads need only a known caller; list_tiers also needs a live one (org._require_live), and list_orgs, which runs inside the agent write cycle, takes the halt and killswitch refusals too. Pinned for the successful reads.

The seven routes are operator routes behind the desktop TokenGate (engine/launch.py): an agent credential is refused 401, and the operator acts as the user (ledger actor USER). repair-rename is the exception: its body names an actor (default the user) that must be the user or the renamed identity itself (Org.repair_rename_identity). account-assign leaves every account check to supervisor.assign_account's shared validator, so being the user does not bypass the account rules. Pinned for the 401 and the refusals; the actor rule of repair-rename is source.

lifecycle.operator-scope (POST /api/orgs/{slug}/nodes/{nid}/scope, P01 F3): the operator retools a node as the user (Org.set_scope with actor USER); a kiosk visitor's raise_ceiling is ignored (source). Pinned by tests/test_state_requests_boundary.py.

Every write-cycle tool (retool, retire, dissolve, cheap_compact, rehire, move, swap, self_subjugate, switch_model and list_orgs) loads the org document under DOC_LOCK through store.write_org (the resident write cycle); rename loads it under supervisor.rename_node's own DOC_LOCK, and list_tiers reads the shared snapshot (store.cached_org). Before the lock, retire and dissolve load the org once more for their authority pre-guard. Source.

Reads outside the org document: list_orgs loads EVERY org's whole document to build the catalogue (store.list_orgs over _scan_orgs, which parses each org; only a summary row per org is kept and kiosk orgs are dropped; relayed from P02's F1 probe, which measured statements on every other org's store, and checked in source) and the mail hub roster (net.remote_peers); list_tiers reads provider discovery (_tier_discovery_payload, machine state behind its own cache, outside the lock); rename reads the turn state of every generation (supervisor.state) and refuses a busy one; switch_model reads the live busy state and the account registry (check_switch_account); a retool naming an account reads the registry (registry.validate_selection); compact reads the turn state and the org killswitch. Source; which of these contacts are org-local is the open instrumentation question.
lifecycle.operator-scope loads the org in the resident write cycle (store.write_org) and reads the node's effective effort before an effort change (source).

Measured with the committed document read cold (changed top-level sections): rename writes nodes, events and the renamed seat's notices (lifecycle.renamed); retool writes nodes and events (set_scope), and access.scope_changed to a target other than the caller; retire writes nodes and events, plus lifecycle.retired to the parent and peers other than the caller; dissolve writes nodes and events and lifecycle.dissolved to the parent and peers other than the caller (the dissolved subtree is told nothing); cheap_compact writes nodes (a knowledge bearer row nid@gen, a fresh session id, generation + 1), events, and the seat's own notices (its backlog folded into a context.notice_digest, then lifecycle.cheap_compacted); rehire writes nodes and events and lifecycle.rehired to the seat and to a parent and peers other than the caller; move writes nodes, events and lifecycle.moved to the old parent, the new parent and the node; swap writes nodes, events and lifecycle.seat_swapped to both parties and their reports; self_subjugate writes nodes, events and lifecycle.subtree_promoted to the new parent, the peers and the promoted target; switch_model writes nodes, events and lifecycle.model_switched to the node. Every changed notices section also changes notice_log. Pinned by tests/test_state_lifecycle_boundary.py against docs/state-system/lifecycle-boundary.json.

No-ops and refusals write nothing: a retire of an already archived node, a rehire of a live node, a move to the current parent (result moved: false, changed: false) and a switch to the tier the node already runs; every refusal discards the unsaved document. The exception is a rehire with `name`: its rename runs before the transaction and survives a later refusal (source, as for staffing in rehire mode). A keyed call adds op_receipts and op_receipts_meta in the same save, except rename, list_orgs and list_tiers, which file no receipt. Pinned.

Routes: reorder writes only nodes (the siblings' ui_order reindexed; no event, no notice); dissolve-all dissolves every top-level seat in ONE save (nodes, one dissolve event per top-level seat, notices); account-assign writes the node's account binding through supervisor.assign_account; compact starts supervisor.manual_compact on a daemon thread and answers {started: true} before that thread writes anything (the fork, the successor session and the archived self are the thread's writes); lineage recover and drop-phantom write through supervisor.recover_lost_generation and drop_phantom_generation under DOC_LOCK; repair-rename moves documents[].node and the current-identity work-item fields and adds one rename_repair log line. Pinned for reorder, dissolve-all, the compact start and every refusal (which writes nothing); the account, lineage and repair success paths are source (they need a registered account, on-disk session files and a stranded record).
lifecycle.operator-scope writes nodes, events and access.scope_changed to the node; a refusal writes nothing. Pinned by tests/test_state_requests_boundary.py.

Tool refusals (422 unless stated): rename 'the name X is already taken'; retool 'you may not rewrite your OWN charter' and granting a tool the caller does not hold ('… cannot grant it'); retire by the caller itself with live reports; move batches whose element is not an object with new_parent ('moves[i] must be an object …'); self_subjugate whose target is not a live descendant ('… is not a live descendant …'); switch_model to an unknown tier (the refusal lists the known tiers). Open background tasks refuse retire, dissolve and cheap_compact (source). Pinned, except the background-task refusals.

Not refused, by the design motto: a retire of a node that is already archived (freed 0, '… was already archived — nothing to do'); a superior retiring a node with live reports gets a dissolve with a warning ('… retire became dissolve'); a rehire of a live node, a move to the current parent (for ANY caller: the no-op answers before the authority check, legacy defect 7) and a switch to the current tier succeed as no-ops with a warning. A switch asked for while the node is mid-turn is QUEUED (pending_switch) rather than applied, and asking for the current tier while one is queued cancels it (source). Pinned, except the queue.

Route refusals (422 unless stated): reorder with no sibling as before= or after=; compact of a node with no conversation yet (and, from source, of a node not live, a knowledge bearer, one just compacted, and 409 for remote control, a freeze, a halt, the killswitch or a busy turn); lineage recover of a row that is not a lost generation; drop-phantom of a row that is not a LOST one; repair-rename with no allowlist; account-assign naming an account that is not registered. Pinned for each named refusal; the other compact refusals are source.
lifecycle.operator-scope takes set_scope's refusals, e.g. an unknown org_visibility ('org_visibility must be one of …'). Pinned by tests/test_state_requests_boundary.py.

Every tool's ledger mutation runs under DOC_LOCK in one load-mutate-save window; three pieces sit outside it: the pre-archive interrupt of retire and dissolve, the filesystem moves and warm-process kills of rename (before its own save), and compact's daemon thread. move batches, swap and self_subjugate validate every refusal before their first write and roll back to a snapshot on a late refusal (source).

facts: Coverage classes (opreceipts.coverage): retire and dissolve PRE (their pre-archive interrupt runs before the lock); rehire TX_POST, or PRE when it carries `name`; retool and switch_model TX_POST; move, swap and self_subjugate TX; cheap_compact UNROLLED (the transcript copy inside the lock); rename, list_orgs and list_tiers NONE. A keyed call files its receipt in the same save as the effect; a replay of a filed key answers the replay envelope (replayed, op_id, outcome applied, the receipt) and writes and broadcasts nothing. The routes take no operation key. Pinned per tool.

Retained result fields follow the per-tool allowlist, scalars only (opreceipts.result_slice). Recorded legacy defect: several allowlists name fields the result never carries, so the receipt keeps nothing — retire and dissolve keep (archived, node) but return freed, nodes and warnings; move keeps (moved), which only the no-op result carries; retool keeps (node, started, account) but returns scope; swap keeps (swapped), whose value is a list. What is kept: cheap_compact node and old_session, rehire node and started, switch_model queued, self_subjugate promoted, demoted and parent. Pinned.

Recorded legacy behaviour: rename returns before admission, so a keyed rename is executed with its key unexamined — a malformed op_key is not refused and no receipt is filed, and a lost answer cannot be looked up. Pinned.
lifecycle.operator-scope files no receipt and takes no key. Pinned by tests/test_state_requests_boundary.py.

retire and dissolve call supervisor.interrupt_before_archive BEFORE the transaction, after only an authority pre-guard: it interrupts the target's in-flight turn and every live descendant's and waits for the turn boundary. Recorded legacy defect: a call refused after that point has already interrupted the target — pinned for a self-retire with live reports and for a keyed retire whose op_key is refused at admission.

After the save: retire, dissolve and cheap_compact call supervisor.remote_reap(slug); cheap_compact calls supervisor.export_predecessor_transcript(org, node, old_sid, reason='cheap_compact') inside the lock; a rehire whose seat has waiting mail drives it once (supervisor.send_message, mail_ping, no ping_reason; the result says RUNNING), and otherwise nothing is driven and the result says IDLE. Recorded legacy defect: the post-save reap names orgtree_rename but the rename branch returns before it, so a rename never reaps. Pinned. From source: a cross-provider switch copies the transcript the same way and wakes a node whose stale freeze it cleared (drive_unfrozen_by_switch); a retool changing effort sends it live (send_live_effort); an account choice on retool or switch_model notifies after the save.

Every accepted write-cycle call ends with exactly one hub_changed, including the no-ops (a rehire of a live node, a move to the current parent, a switch to the current tier) and list_orgs. Recorded legacy behaviour: list_orgs is a read that takes the write lock, saves and broadcasts. A replay broadcasts nothing. rename and list_tiers never call hub_changed; rename's broadcast is supervisor.notify(slug, new, 'renamed', …) after its own save. rename also kills the parked warm process of every generation (warmpool.kill_node) and moves the scratch directory and the CLI project directory before the save, rolling them back if the save fails (source). Pinned for the broadcasts.

Routes: reorder, dissolve-all, lineage recover and drop-phantom and repair-rename end with hub_changed (account-assign awaits hub.changed, source); compact starts a daemon thread running supervisor.manual_compact and broadcasts nothing itself. Recorded legacy behaviour: dissolve-all tells each later top-level seat that an earlier one was dissolved (lifecycle.dissolved, relation peer) and then dissolves it in the same save. Pinned, except account-assign.

lifecycle.operator-scope makes NO explicit hub_changed call (store.save_org announces the write, source); an effort change is sent to a running turn after the save (send_live_effort). Pinned by tests/test_state_requests_boundary.py.

orgtree_rehire, orgtree_retire, orgtree_dissolve and orgtree_cheap_compact are managed-wait tools (mcptool.MANAGED_WAIT_TOOLS): every call, refusals included, journals in the tool_waits sidecar, outside the org document (relayed from P02's F1 probe; source: the managed-wait wrapper).

The agent door labels each call for the storage census (stateprobe.refine('tool:' + tool)); the routes are labelled by the access middleware. P02's per-operation record covers most of the family (below).

Observed by the P02 per-operation probe (tools/p02_operation_contacts.py; docs/state-system/p02-operation-contacts.md) (synthetic data, v3 bfbc4ae): a loss-accounted per-operation record for every lifecycle and catalogue contract cold and warm, with the variants, keyed calls (fresh, replay, malformed key) and refusals, and lifecycle.operator-scope (P01 F3) cold, warm and a refusal. No row makes an unknown contact. Org-level locality: only catalogue.list-orgs reads other orgs' stores, as declared; agent-level locality stays within each row's declared set, and every refusal writes nothing and changes no agent's mail. The control control:lifecycle-third-agent is flagged. NOT covered: the success paths of lifecycle.account-assign, lifecycle.lineage-recover and lifecycle.lineage-drop-phantom, which have refusal rows only (question below). Native negative controls are the P03 gate, not a clause of this legacy facet (S2d decision 1, reviewer ruling on 803227e). Asserted by tests/test_state_p02_contact_facets.py.

orgtree_ask, orgtree_request_scope, orgtree_present and orgtree_submit_report act for the calling agent itself. The gate is the user-mail gate: a top-level agent, or the holder of a user audience, reaches the user directly. Anyone else has an ask or a scope request ROUTED to its superior as mail rather than refused; a presentation is REFUSED ('presenting a document needs a DIRECT user audience …'); and a report is forwarded to the superior as a request with no presentation. orgtree_withdraw_ask withdraws only the caller's own open ask. Pinned by tests/test_state_requests_boundary.py against docs/state-system/requests-boundary.json for a top-level and a deep caller of each.

POST /api/orgs/{slug}/asks/{aid}/answer and POST /api/orgs/{slug}/nodes/{nid}/batch are operator routes behind the desktop TokenGate: the user answers or dismisses one ask by id, or resolves a node's whole request batch (question tabs, the credits tab and the scope items) in one submit. Pinned.

From source: the tools load the org under DOC_LOCK in the agent write cycle; the user-mail gate reads the caller's parent and its user audience (_has_audience); the answer route reads the ask by id and its revision; the batch route reads the node's open ask, its pending credit request and its pending scope request and their revisions; a report's artifact citations are read from the docket (_report_artifact_refs).

Measured with the committed document read cold: a top-level ask writes asks and events; a deep ask writes the question as mail to the superior (mail, mail_log, lifecycle, nodes, events). A withdraw writes asks and events, and a withdraw with nothing open writes nothing. A presentation writes documents and events. A deep report writes the forwarding request mail to the superior (mail, mail_log, lifecycle, nodes, events); a top-level report writes documents, events, lifecycle and the user's inbox (user_inbox). A top-level scope request writes scope_requests and events; a deep one is routed like an ask. The answer route writes the ask's state, the answer as user mail to the asker (mail, mail_log, lifecycle, nodes), user_outbox and events, a dismissal the same; the batch route writes the same for an ask-only batch. Refusals write nothing. Pinned by tests/test_state_requests_boundary.py against docs/state-system/requests-boundary.json.

'a question is required'; 'items must be a non-empty list'; a deep presentation (above); an answer against a stale card revision ('the card changed after it rendered (answer against revision N, card at M) …'); a batch against a stale revision ('… a request was appended or amended …') and a batch for a node with nothing open ('X has no open request batch'). From source: a report needs a title and a body. Pinned by tests/test_state_requests_boundary.py against docs/state-system/requests-boundary.json, except the report clause.

Each tool is one whole-document write cycle under DOC_LOCK in the agent door; each route one load-mutate-save under the lock. The card revisions are compare-and-set stamps checked under the lock (source).

facts: request: the requester's target must be one of its superiors or the user (a headless org refuses a user target, source); forward: the node the request currently awaits, or the user; grant: a superior grants an audience with itself, and a delegated grant may open its own ear, a live peer's or its direct superior's for a grantee in its subtree; the user's authority is unconditional; deny: the node holding the request; revoke: the grant's anchor (source). POST /api/orgs/{slug}/audiences acts as the user; GET /api/orgs/{slug}/audiences is an operator read. Pinned by tests/test_state_requests_boundary.py against docs/state-system/requests-boundary.json, except the headless and revoke clauses.

From source: the chain from requester to target (is_ancestor, parent), the open audience_requests row, the audiences list and the live peers; the list route loads the org without the lock (store.load_org) and returns audiences and requests as stored.

Measured cold: request writes audience_requests and the request mail to the next hop (mail, mail_log, lifecycle, nodes, events); forward moves the request and mails the next hop; an agent's grant writes audiences, resolves the request and mails the decision to the grantee; deny resolves the request and mails the decision; revoke writes audiences and tells the grantee (access.audience_changed); the operator route's grant writes audiences, audience_requests and access.audience_changed to both parties, and no mail. A request to the direct superior writes nothing (already reachable). Refusals write nothing. Pinned by tests/test_state_requests_boundary.py against docs/state-system/requests-boundary.json.

A request whose target is not in the requester's chain is refused; one aimed at the direct superior succeeds as a no-op ('you can already message them'); an unknown action is refused on the tool ('action must be request|forward|grant|deny|revoke') and on the route ('action must be grant|deny|revoke'). From source: the agent-door tools read the org in the write cycle (interrupt, unstick, the restart gates) or under their own DOC_LOCK (halt, unhalt, continue_on); interrupt reads the node's live turn state (supervisor.state: its process, codex or antigravity turn, admission and deploy-hold waits); halt reads the runtime owners of the node's turns; continue_on makes a LIVE provider read of the target account's capacity outside the lock (_continue_on_account); restart_wake reads its machine-wide sidecar (restart-wakes file under the data root); prime_restart status reads the machine-wide prime file; steer reads the node's steer store; steer-state reads the node's runtime state; resume reads every frozen node.

Measured cold. halt writes nodes (the halt record, phase halting then halted) and events; unhalt writes nodes and events, and leaves an unsaved empty steer_attempts owner for the node on the cached org document, which the next save writes (so a keyed unhalt's own receipt save writes steer_attempts; see the legacy defect below), and unhalt of a node that is not halted writes nothing; unstick of a frozen node writes nodes, events and policy.unstuck to the node, and of a node that is not stuck writes nothing ('… not stuck — nothing to release'); interrupt, continue_on (its switch is _continue_on_account's own two transactions, source), steer, steer-ack, steer-state, process, resume with nothing frozen and remote-control write nothing to the org document here; the killswitch latch writes killswitch and events (and pauses every armed watchdog in the same save), its release pops killswitch and writes events, and a release while nothing is latched writes nothing. restart_wake arm, cancel and status write NO org section: the wake lives in its own sidecar file. Non-desktop restart tools: self_restart and prime_restart arm or cancel write events (the gate's log row). The kiosk handler (non-desktop) writes kiosk (enable, token rotation, caps). Recorded legacy defect (docket unhalting-an-agent-leaves-an-unsaved-empty-steer; found by P02's SQL-level write trace, reproduced by P01): halt.unhalt calls supervisor.scan_steer_records, which loads the cached (resident) document under the document lock and creates steer_attempts[node] = {} with setdefault, and does not save when no attempt is pending; the lock-release discard check does not catch that change, so on the warm document every later save on the org, whatever its operation and whoever calls it, deletes that owner's steer_attempts rows again until a later unhalt, and the durable document ends with the empty owner. A reload between the calls drops the carry-over. Pinned by tests/test_state_control_boundary.py against docs/state-system/control-boundary.json.

prime_restart and restart_wake: an action other than arm, cancel or status is refused ('action must be arm|cancel|status'); every falsy action (omitted, null, empty, 0, false) arms, because the door reads str(a.get('action') or 'arm'), and the selectors use that same reading (action normalization str_or_arm), so it selects the arm contract, while an unknown action ('bogus', 'ARM', ' arm', 1) selects no contract and the door refuses it; restart_wake refuses a mode other than one_shot. remote-control: the action must be start or stop. process: an unknown node is 404. resume: 409 while the killswitch is latched ('release it before resuming'). kiosk (non-desktop): the org must already be a kiosk, and a credits cap below the current top-level holdings is refused ('cap below current holdings …'). Pinned by tests/test_state_control_boundary.py against docs/state-system/control-boundary.json.

facts: PROFILES (decision 1 on p01-f2-contracts-for-the-run-control-entry-point). Under the desktop-managed profile (ORGTREE_DESKTOP_MANAGED=1, which engine/launch.py sets, and under which it installs desktop_maintenance) orgtree_self_relaunch, orgtree_prime_relaunch arm and cancel and the deprecated orgtree_self_update take the machine-wide gate (Org.self_restart_gate and Org.prime_restart_gate): only a top-level agent or a holder of a user audience, any other caller refused 422 ('a self-restart restarts the shared orgtree install for EVERY org on this machine …' or 'a primed restart …'). prime_relaunch status takes no gate and needs only a live caller (an archived seat is refused 403 'authenticated seat is archived or replaced …'). Under the non-desktop profile orgtree_self_relaunch and orgtree_prime_relaunch are refused 422 at the door whatever their action or options ('<tool> is available only to the desktop-managed V2 profile'), while orgtree_self_update takes the same gate as orgtree_self_restart. The frozen deployment profile refuses all three 403 before any write, prime_relaunch status included, under either profile ('the frozen deployment profile disables agent-triggered self-update, self-restart, and primed restart …'). A halted caller, or any caller while the org killswitch is latched, is refused 409 before any tool runs (the shared door gate, source; pinned for the run-control tools by tests/test_state_control_boundary.py). Pinned by tests/test_state_relaunch_boundary.py against docs/state-system/relaunch-boundary.json.

Under the desktop-managed profile self_relaunch, prime_relaunch arm and self_update first read the machine-wide request file <DATA_ROOT>/desktop-maintenance.json under desktop_maintenance's lock: a request that is pending or acknowledged is returned as it stands (armed true, already_armed true, and the whole request: its action, target, reason, by_org and by_node, which may be another org's) and no new request is written. prime_relaunch status reads only a pending request (desktop_maintenance.pending) and names its by_org, by_node and arming time; cancel reads the pending request. The gates read the caller's node and its audiences. Pinned by tests/test_state_relaunch_boundary.py against docs/state-system/relaunch-boundary.json.

Desktop-managed profile: every admitted call except status appends one org event in this request's save: self_relaunch and self_update 'self_restart' with detail {} (no reason is recorded), prime_relaunch arm 'prime_restart_arm' with {target: 'org', reason} and cancel 'prime_restart_cancel' with {}. The event is appended even when nothing new is requested (already_armed) and when nothing is cancelled (cancelled false, which includes an acknowledged request: cancel leaves it untouched). Outside the org document the maintenance adapter writes <DATA_ROOT>/desktop-maintenance.json (a temporary file then os.replace, source): a new request {id, action, target, reason, by_org, by_node, at, state: 'pending'} with action 'restart' and target 'org' for self_relaunch and prime arm, and action 'update' with the caller's target for self_update; cancel rewrites a pending request to state 'cancelled' with cancelled_by. status writes nothing. Every refusal writes nothing, including self_update's refused target, which is refused after the gate has run and so drops the gate's event with the request's save. Non-desktop profile: self_update appends the 'self_restart' event, with {force: true, reason} followed by 'self_restart_forced' on the forced path, and writes nothing else here; the relaunch tools write nothing. Keyed calls also write op_receipts and op_receipts_meta. Pinned by tests/test_state_relaunch_boundary.py against docs/state-system/relaunch-boundary.json.

The door reads prime_relaunch's action as str(a.get('action') or 'arm') and refuses anything but arm, cancel and status 422 ('action must be arm|cancel|status'); the selectors use that same reading (action normalization str_or_arm), so every falsy action selects the arm contract and an unknown action ('nope', 'ARM') selects none. _desktop_relaunch_args admits only reason for self_relaunch and only action and reason for prime_relaunch, refusing any other option 422 before the gate ('orgtree_self_relaunch accepts only reason; unsupported option(s): target'), so target, force, deadline_minutes and a legacy action on self_relaunch are refused. Under the non-desktop profile the profile refusal comes first, so an extra option draws the same 'available only to the desktop-managed V2 profile'. self_update is not checked by _desktop_relaunch_args: under the desktop-managed profile force is refused 422 ('Desktop maintenance waits for idle; force is unavailable') and a target outside org, mailhub and both is refused 422 by the adapter ('invalid desktop maintenance target/action'); under the non-desktop profile a forced call needs a reason (422 'a FORCED self-restart requires a `reason` …') and takes the forced path. Pinned by tests/test_state_relaunch_boundary.py against docs/state-system/relaunch-boundary.json.

The maintenance request is one machine-wide file guarded by a lock local to the engine process and written outside the org document's transaction: the org event and the request are two separate writes, and a pending request made by one org is returned to, and cancellable by, a gated agent of any org on the machine (source).

facts: Every route is an operator route behind the desktop TokenGate that both current launch paths install (engine/launch.py load_app): a request with no credential is refused 401 ('missing authentication; provide a desktop or live agent credential'), and an agent credential on a route 401 ('agent credential is invalid or expired; reconnect the agent session'); past the gate a route acts as the user. orgtree_send_file and orgtree_send_file_once are agent tools on the agent door, acting for the calling agent on files it can reach. The public kiosk gateway, which the desktop launcher does not start, is read from source: GET /api/orgs lists only the token's org there, the org_inbox upload and send routes refuse it 404 ('not found'), and node upload is reachable through it. GET /api/orgs reads every org's document once (store.list_orgs_with_docs) and each org's working count; a kiosk org's admin row carries kiosk_cfg, share token included. The org inbox list reads a snapshot of org_inbox (the last 100 entries with total and unread); the mail item route reads its box's sections and searches the box whole, so found false is an answer. The reply-events count reads the reply_events sidecar read-only. Pinned by tests/test_state_exchange_boundary.py against docs/state-system/exchange-boundary.json.

A delivered @org: send writes, in the destination org, org_inbox, mail, mail_log, notices, notice_log, events, nodes and audiences (post_external_mail bootstraps an audience holder) and copies attachments into every recipient's uploads/. org_inbox read writes org_inbox_read. org_inbox upload writes a staged file under <DATA_ROOT>/net_stage, named by a map held in process memory and pruned after 24 hours. org_inbox send writes this org's org_inbox (an out entry) and, for @org:, the OTHER org's documents, a write across two orgs; for @net: it appends to the mail-hub spool (source). inbox clear moves user_inbox into user_mail_log. node upload writes the file under the node's scratch uploads/, de-duplicating a name with -2. The reply-events DELETE deletes the node's rows from the reply_events sidecar and writes nodes (a new reply_incarnation). retract writes mail and tombstones the entry in mail_log. Pinned by tests/test_state_exchange_boundary.py against docs/state-system/exchange-boundary.json.

orgtree_send_file writes outbox/ only, never an org section, and with a delivery_id also a row in the machine-wide <DATA_ROOT>/file-deliveries.db and the copy under outbox/delivery-<identity>/, replayed as the same result for the same file and caption; orgtree_send_file_once requires the delivery_id and is then the same call. Every refusal writes nothing to any org. Pinned by tests/test_state_exchange_boundary.py against docs/state-system/exchange-boundary.json.
